summary: The Trustees decided to write to the National Parks Service about the unresolved responsibility for maintaining the Nielsen Park wharf, noting that lack of repairs could endanger the public and that public-risk insurance should be addressed.
counterparty: National Parks Service and Maritime Services Board
red_flag_reason: The wharf's maintenance responsibility was unresolved, repairs were lacking, and the Trustees warned that deterioration could endanger public safety.
quote:
The question of the wharf at Nielsen Park was
discussed and it was decided that a letter be sent
to the National Parks Service expressing concern at
the delay in the Service and the Maritime Services
Board coming to an agreement as to the responsibility
for maintaining the wharf. It was pointed out that
the Trustees are strongly of the opinion that the
retention of the Nielsen Park wharf in good repair is
very much in the public interest, and that the lack of
repairs to the wharf is likely to result in such
deterioration of the entire structure that the safety
of the public will be endangered. Moreover, the
Trustees consider that the Service should call for
expert advice as to the present condition of the
wharf as a matter of urgency. The question of public
risk in regard to persons receiving an injury whilst
on the wharf was raised and Mr.Miller offered to
communicate with the Transport and General Insurance
in regard to this matter.

asset: four chairs and one wall mirror
summary: Mr. Yelland reported that four chairs and one wall mirror from the late Madame Florence Austral's estate might be loaned to Vaucluse House to furnish the upper corridor, and the furniture had been stored in Gilberthorpe's Room for inspection.
quote:
Mr.Yelland reported that, at the last meeting of the
Opera House Trust of which he is a member, the
question arose of the disposal of four chairs and one
wall mirror bequeathed some years ago from the estate
of the late Madame Florence Austral. As the Trustees
of the Opera House Trust had no area in which these
could be displayed, Mr.Yelland suggested that,subject
to the approval of the Trustees of Vaucluse House,the
chairs and mirror might be loaned to Vaucluse House,
thereby contributing to the furnishing of upper
corridor. He had contacted the President who
considered the furniture, being of the right period,
would be most suitable.for this corridor. The
furniture had arrived during the week and was stored
in Gilberthorpe's Room for the Trustees' inspection.

Blue-Mountains project in the coach house
display area. The committee hoped to
commence an extensive drive for new
membership in the near future;

asset: timber joists and ceilings in bedrooms and corridors
summary: Replacing timber joists and new ceilings in bedrooms and corridors affected by white ant damage was estimated at about $1,000, and a letter pointing this out was agreed to be sent to the National Parks Service.
red_flag_reason: White ant damage required replacement of timber joists and new ceilings
quote:
(3) The cost of replacing timber joists and
new ceilings in bedrooms and corridors
affected by white ant damage, was in the
vicinity of $1,000. He considered that,
had the Service chosen a reputable firm
to attend to the white ant problem, the
activity found in these rooms would have
been detected two years ago, whereas the
person doing the treatment, being in
business on his own, did not have the
necessary equipment for detection. It was
agreed that a letter pointing out this
fact be sent to the National Parks
Service.

summary: The Trust agreed to ask Mr. K.R. Doyle to support nominations of Mr. Peter Cook or Mr. Max Herford as a replacement trustee.
counterparty: Mr. K.R. Doyle; Mr. Peter Cook; Mr. Max Herford
quote:
(i) Director, National Parks Service, in reply
to Trust's letter of 16th.October addressed
to the Minister, requesting an appointment
of a Trustee replacing Mr.J.A.Kelly and
informing Trust "that the present procedure
when appointing new Trustees is for the
Minister to seek the concurrence of the local
Member of the Legislative Assembly before
approving of an appointment", and suggested
the Trust furnish nominations to the Member
for Vaucluse, Mr.K.R.Doyle, seeking his
support to such nomination (s). It was agreed
that a letter be sent to Mr.Doyle,nominating
Mr.Peter Cook and or Mr.Max Herford, and
informing him that neither of these gentlemen
had been approached by the Trust, but that the
Trust considered they had the necessary
qualifications and requesting Mr.Doyle's
support.

Council expires in December this year and
nominations are being called for. It was
resolved that the Trust nominate Captain
P.Lusher and inform the Minister that this
nomination was not submitted in criticism of
the present representative,Hon.W.J.Holt,M.L.C.,
but as an indication of Trust's interest in
the Council.

Tabling of Financial Allocation for 72/73. The
Secretary drew attention to the amount of $6,725
allocated for Maintenance and Protection,informing
Trustees that, of this amount, $1,725 had already
been paid for removal of platforms and replacing
pile at Nielsen Park; $1,000 towards replacing
timbers and plaster ceilings in Vaucluse House for
damage caused by white ants, and that $3,000 was
allowed by the Service towards the Trust's program
of painting jobs needed at Nielsen Park. It was
agreed that the most urgent works at Nielsen Park were
the painting of exterior and interior of Nielsen Kiosk
and fences, and that Contato's quotation for this
work be accepted.

summary: Mr. Carter reported that the Blue Mountains project was deferred to February or March next year, and the meeting resolved to ask the Director for urgent attention.

communication with Mr.Carter of the Service in regard

informed him that,because of other commitments,this
project had been deferred to February or March of next
year. It was resolved that a letter be sent to the
Director,requesting that this project be given urgent
attention, as the Trustees considered that in order to
retain the enthusiastic support of the Friends the
project should be accomplished at an early date,so
that,one project being accomplished others,which are
in mind by the Friends, can follow.

summary: The Secretary/Manager could not yet submit a detailed formal report on Nielsen Park operations and recommended continuing observation and gradual tightening-up before drastic action.
red_flag_reason: The Secretary/Manager described the Nielsen Park situation as incredibly complex and recommended extreme caution before drastic action.
quote:
In conclusion, whilst on the one hand I regret that I am
not yet in a position to submit a detailed formal report upon the survey the
Trust has instructed me to carry out upon Nielsen Park operations, this is
not due to any dereliction of duty but rather to caution. All I would like to
say on this subject at this stage is that I find the whole situation an
incredibly complex one and its very complexity convinces me that there is a
need to proceed with extreme caution. Particularly is this so when, whatever
faults there may be, Nielsen Park at least continues to function in that it is
currently open daily for those who wish to use it and I must say that to do
anything drastic at this stage of the 1972/73 swimming season and thus perhaps
precipitate a crisis would be folly indeed. My own view is that the best (and
for that matter the fairest) plan, is for me to continue my present observations,
to continue the gradual "tightening up" process which is currently taking place
and for the whole matter to be reviewed during the Winter months in time to
allow:-

summary: Concerns about hooliganism and vandalism in Nielsen Park were addressed by appointing a special sub-committee and discussing police action against a traced offender.
counterparty: Mr. and Mrs. J.F. Richardson; Mr. Barrett; Mr. Pierce; Mr. Hobson; Ranger Westbrook
red_flag_reason: Increasing hooliganism and vandalism in Nielsen Park, including a youth smashing through fencing and driving around the paddock, required a special sub-committee and police action.
quote:
The President read a letter which had been received from
Mr. and Mrs. J.F. Richardson of 14, Greycliffe Avenue
expressing deep concern at increasing hooliganism and
vandalism in the Park, especially late at night. They
attach no blame to the staff at Nielsen Park for whom they
expressed nothing but praise for their vigilance and
courage. After some discussion it was agreed that a special
sub-committee be appointed to look into the whole matter,
consisting of Messrs. Barrett, Pierce and Hobson. The
Secretary/Manager undertook to write a suitable letter of
appreciation to Mr. and Mrs. Richardson for their comments:
he also advised the Meeting that, with the help of the police,
one youth who had smashed through fencing and driven his
vehicle round and round the paddock adjacent to Greycliffe
Avenue at 2.30 a.m. on Sunday, 14th July, 1974 had been
traced. Ranger Westbrook was discussing with the police
what action should be taken against the offender.

(c) Dispute with M.W.S. & D. Board re water charges, Steel Point Cottage.

The Secretary/Manager presented a letter from the Secretary of the Board advising that as a result of negotiations carried on in recent months they had decided to cancel all back claims for payment of water rate based on rateable value and to charge on a consumption basis only. This decision resulted in us receiving a cheque to the value of $21.23 to offset the overcharge made on the consumption basis since 1969. The Trust agreed that this was a very satisfactory conclusion to a difference of opinion with the Board which had existed over a period of four years.

summary: The Trustees discussed a restaurant lease and liquor licence, noting favourable ministerial and police views subject to additional toilet facilities, and agreed to seek an amendment to the N.P. & W.S. Act with lease safeguards if needed.
counterparty: Minister for Lands; Sergeant Windsor; Licencing Branch of the Police at Waverley
quote:
The major part of the discussion revolved around the
possibility of obtaining a liquor licence. Mr. Finlay
and Mr. Doyle had tentatively discussed this matter with
the Minister for Lands who had indicated that any
application would receive his favourable consideration.
Mr. Finlay quoted from a letter which he had already
written to the President, indicating that all that would
be required would be a restaurant licence which did not
necessitate liquor being on sale for a minimum of ten
hours per day. In fact, this type of licence would allow
liquor to be sold between noon and 3 p.m. each day with
a further hour permitted for "drinking up time". He
also advised that it would be possible, by an alteration
to Section 168 of the N.P. & W.S. Act for a ministerial
licence to be granted. The Secretary/Manager further
advised that he had a visit from Sergeant Windsor and
a colleague of the Licencing Branch of the Police at
Waverley, who indicated that there would be no objections
from their Branch to a proposed licence, providing that
additional toilet accommodation was provided adjacent
to the restaurant consisting of one washbowl and a
toilet for ladies and a washbowl, toilet and urinal
for gentlemen. There would be no difficulty in pro-
viding this accommodation as a sewer line already
exists for the staff toilet in the premises.

summary: The Trust agreed to draw up a lease for the Gardener's Cottage using the previous employee-lease format with nominal rental of $1 per week.
quote:
Having considered previous leases granted to employees,
Mr. Finlay advised that he saw no reason to alter the
format and it was agreed that a lease should be drawn
up and that the nominal rental would be $1 per week.

summary: The Trust confirmed that the President should engage Mr. Clive Lucas for the architectural survey with tight terms and an initial expenditure limit of $2,500, with possible drafting help from Mr. R. Rowe.
counterparty: Mr. Clive Lucas; Mr. R. Rowe
quote:
The President reported the findings of the sub-com-
mittee dealing with this matter and recommended that
Mr. Clive Lucas should be engaged to carry out the sur-
vey. Whilst agreeing with the recommendation, Mr.
Herford indicated that he personally, would object to
any architect being given an open cheque. All mem-
bers present agreed with his sentiments and it was
confirmed that the President should write a suitable
letter engaging Mr. Lucas with a limitation on initial
expenditure of $2,500. Mr. Cook expressed the view
that our terms of reference should be as tight as poss-
ible and the President assured the Meeting that this
would be borne in mind when writing the letter. He
further indicated that draft of the letter would be
read to Mr. Finlay for any legal comment, and that if

summary: The Secretary/Manager's report was accepted and the Trust approved Wormald Bros.' quotation for a fire-alarm system, instructing negotiation with the Service about financing.
quote:
The report having been previously circulated was
accepted and it was agreed that the quotation re-
ceived from Wormald Bros. for the installation of a
fire alarm system for the House should be accepted and
the Secretary/Manager was instructed to negotiate with
the Service regarding the financing of this project.

summary: Recoup summaries Nos. 59 to 64 were formally confirmed by the Board after being passed for payment and reimbursed by N.P. & W.S.
quote:
Recoup summaries Nos. 59 - 64 were tabled. These had
already been passed for payment and re-imbursed by the
N.P. & W.S. and were formally confirmed by the Board.

summary: The President congratulated Mr. K.R. Doyle on election as President of the Friends of Vaucluse House and expressed appreciation for Mr. Harold Snelling's leadership.
counterparty: Mr. K.R. Doyle; Mr. Harold Snelling
quote:
The President congratulated Mr. K.R. Doyle on his
election as President of the Friends of Vaucluse House
and then expressed the Trust's great appreciation of the
leadership of the "Friends", since it was formed, by the
retiring President, Mr. Harold Snelling.

summary: Mr. Doyle said the Friends should concentrate on raising money for special projects with strong public-relations value.
counterparty: Mr. Doyle; Friends of Vaucluse House
quote:
Some discussion of the future activities of the
"Friends" then took place and Mr. Doyle indicated
that he would encourage them to concentrate on raising
money for special projects with the accent on programmes
having as much public relations value as possible.

summary: Storm damage at Nielsen Park was examined, but action on the wharf area was deferred pending N.P. & W.S. recommendations while the public was warned that the area was dangerous.
counterparty: Engineering Section of N.P. & W.S.; Mr. George King
red_flag_reason: No action could be taken on the dangerous wharf area until N.P. & W.S. made definite recommendations, and full compliance with warnings was difficult without a permanent attendant.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that this had been examined
by the Engineering Section of the N.P. & W.S. and by the
Assistant Director, Mr. George King. The Meeting agreed
that until definite recommendations were received from
the N.P. & W.S. regarding the wharf area no action could
be taken apart from warning the public that the area was
dangerous. The Secretary/Manager advised that the neces-
sary warning notice had already been erected, but without
a man permanently on duty at the wharf it was extremely
difficult to ensure full compliance with the instructions.

summary: The Trust agreed that damage to the sea wall must be attended to before the swimming season and empowered the Secretary/Manager to deal with it.
quote:
In so far as damage to the sea wall was concerned it
was agreed that this must be attended to before the
opening of the swimming season and the Secretary/Manager
was empowered to deal with this.

summary: Because some members felt admission fees were too low, the Secretary/Manager was asked to discuss increasing charges with N.P. & W.S. and return the item to the August agenda.
quote:
Some members felt that the admission fees were too
low and the Secretary/Manager was requested to have
discussions regarding the increasing of charges with
the Head Office of N.P. & W.S. and to put this item on
the agenda for further discussion at the August Meeting.

summary: Mr. K.R. Doyle reported that necessary premium increases with the Government Insurance Office were almost finalised and would be reported at the next meeting.
quote:
Mr. K.R. Doyle advised that he had almost finalised the
necessary premium increases with the Government Insurance
Office and would report further at the next Meeting.

summary: Mr. Cook's proposal to write an article with photographs about Vaucluse House for The Australasian Antique Collector was heartily approved, with him to liaise with the Secretary/Manager.
quote:
As editor of "The Australasian Antique Collector",
Mr. Cook indicated that he would like to write an
article together with suitable photographs about
Vaucluse House. As the proposal was heartily
approved of by the Trustees present it was left for
him to liaise with the Secretary/Manager who would
provide him with as much information as possible.

summary: Mrs. Doris Kearney underwent successful heart-artery surgery and was unlikely to return to work for under two months, while Mrs. Hobson performed her duties.
quote:
Mrs. Doris Kearney entered hospital at the end of the month for
an operation on arteries leading to the heart and I am happy to report,
that this was successful and her surgeons are pleased with the progress
she is making toward recovery. It is, however, unlikely that she will
be able to return to work in under two months. During her absence,
Mrs. Hobson is performing her duties.

summary: The Public Service Board completed its salary and wage review, and new pay scales for Trust employees were put into effect in the pay week ending 31 July 1974.
counterparty: Public Service Board; National Parks and Wildlife Service
quote:
The review of salaries and wages by the Public Service Board was
completed as forecasted in my June report. From job evaluation sheets
compiled by the writer the Board has been able to equate the positions
of Trust employees with similar positions in the National Parks and
Wildlife Service. Most of the pay increases are quite substantial
and will be automatically covered by the Service in our allocations for
the current financial year. With the approval of the President the new
pay scales were put into effect in the pay - week ending 31.7.1974.
Details will be available for perusal by the Trustees at the August
Meeting.

summary: Proposed adjustments to casual-worker rates for the next Nielsen Park season were being worked out by the P.S.B. for consideration at the September Meeting.
quote:
Proposed adjustments to the rates payable to casual workers dur-
ing the next season at Nielsen Park are now being worked out by the
P.S.B. in consultation with the writer and will be put forward for
consideration by the Trust at the September Meeting.

asset: Vaucluse House window panes, Bakery stonework, and wine-cellar stonework
summary: General maintenance included replacing 89 broken or cracked window panes, completing pointing on the Bakery, and replacing eroded stonework in the first wine cellar.
quote:
General maintenance continues. All broken and cracked window
panes in the House and dependencies have been replaced, a total of
eighty-nine pieces of glass. Necessary pointing of stonework on the
Bakery has been completed. In the wine-cellars, eroded stonework to
to the left of the window in the first cellar has been removed and
new stone inserted to match in with existing foundation walls.

summary: Rentokil inspectors found no fresh termite activity, indicating the problem was under control, though previously affected woodwork in the main hall and Guests' Diningroom would be repaired soon.
quote:
During the month Rentokil inspectors carried out their six-
monthly survey of woodwork and furniture. No fresh termite activity
was discovered so it appears that we now have the problem under con-
trol in all buildings. Small areas of previously affected woodwork
in the main hall and the Guests' Diningroom will be made good in the
near future.

summary: After discussions with Mr. John Eagleton of N.P. & W.S. Finance, the Secretary/Manager submitted a formal request for funds to meet the fire-alarm-system expenditure.
quote:
After discussions with Mr. John Eagleton, Head of the Finance
Division of the N.P. & W.S., the writer has submitted a formal re-
quest for funds to meet this expenditure.

summary: All information required by Mr. Cook for the Vaucluse House article had been supplied, and facilities were given to his photographer for special shots.
quote:
All information required by Mr. Cook has been supplied and facil-
ities given to his photographer to take a number of special shots.

summary: Mr. Randall Reed advised that the inventory work was almost completed except for close inspection of certain china pieces in locked display cabinets.
quote:
Mr. Randall Reed has advised the writer that apart from close
inspection of certain pieces of china in locked display cabinets this
work is almost completed.

asset: kitchen area door between scullery and larder/dairy
summary: To aid future security of the kitchen area, the original door between the scullery and larder/dairy area was renovated and re-hung.
quote:
As an aid to the future security of the kitchen area the writer
has had the original door renovated and re-hung between the scullery
and the larder/dairy area.

summary: Renovation of the peripheral park fencing had proceeded well during a month of reasonably good weather.
quote:
Renovation of peripheral park fencing has proceeded well during
a month of reasonably good weather.

summary: Fine weather enabled general clearing, pruning, lawn treatment, and planting of spring flowers, with the gardens expected to improve over the next few weeks.
quote:
A great deal of general clearing, pruning, treatment of lawns
and planting-out of spring flowers has been made possible by the spell
of fine weather. The appearance of the gardens should progressively
improve during the next few weeks.

summary: Internal painting, carpeting, and electrical work at the Gardener's Cottage were complete as far as possible, but occupation awaited an overdue electric cooking stove from Metter's.
red_flag_reason: The cottage could not be ready for occupation until Metter's supplied the electric cooking stove, which was considerably overdue on forecasted delivery.
quote:
All internal painting has been completed. The carpeting has been
laid and the electrical installation finished as far as possible. Once
Metter's supply the Electric Cooking Stove, which is considerably over-
due on forecasted delivery, the cottage will be ready for occupation.

summary: Restaurant-lease advertising had generated strong response and much enquiry-handling, but no reply had yet been received to the President's letter to the Minister about a proposed liquor licence.
quote:
The response to advertisements in the "Wentworth Courier" and
"The Sydney Morning Herald" has, in the writer's opinion, been very
good, and since they appeared, a great deal of the writer's time, in
and out of normal office hours, has been taken up dealing with the
enquiries. To date no reply has been received to the President's
letter to the Minister regarding the proposed Restaurant Liquor Licence.

asset: Nielsen Park sea wall and tunnel entrance
summary: After unsuccessful attempts to obtain contractor quotations, Ranger Westbrook found a concreting contractor willing to repair the sea wall and tunnel entrance for $950, and an order to proceed was being given with the President's approval.
quote:
Certain essential repairs to the sea wall and entrance to the
tunnel are required before the commencement of the swimming season in
October. After a number of unsuccessful attempts to get contractors
to come out and submit a quotation for the work, Ranger Westbrook
approached a man who was doing some concreting at a house in Greycliffe
Avenue. He made a survey and offered to do the job for $950.00. In
the writer's opinion, this is a reasonable figure considering the
amount of work involved and, with the approval of the President, the
contractor is being given an order to proceed. We are still trying
to find someone who is prepared to sink a new pile to replace the one
shifted from its foundations on the south side of the pool area.

asset: Nielsen Park Halbert Pavilion and dressing shed
summary: Mr. Kelly was asked to quote to make the Halbert Pavilion suitable for storing equipment removed from the dressing shed destroyed by gales.

I have also asked Mr. Kelly who renewed the interior woodwork

(a) Making the Halbert Pavilion suitable for the storage of equipment
which had to be removed from the dressing shed destroyed by the gales.
At present this equipment is housed in the main dressing sheds, but
will have to be moved out before the commencement of the swimming season.

We continue to carry out our commitments at Clark Island and
through the good offices of Ranger Westbrook we are now getting the
freshwater tank re-filled, by Fenwick's as required, free of charge -
a saving of some $15.00 per week to the Service.

summary: Twenty-one acceptances had been received for Dr. Cobden Parkes's 14 September function, but no definite decision was reached on a presentation because members thought he might be embarrassed.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager reported that twenty-one accept-
ances for this function on the 14th September, had been
received. Some discussion regarding a presentation to
Dr. Cobden Parkes took place, but no definite decision
was reached as many members felt that Dr. Parkes would
not expect it and, indeed, might be seriously embarassed
if such a presentation was made.

summary: The President confirmed that Professor Ward and Mr. Webber had accepted invitations to act as consultants to the Trust, and Trustees were to be given an opportunity to meet them.
quote:
The President was pleased to confirm that both
Professor Ward of the University of Sydney and Mr.
Webber, the Government Architect, had accepted his
invitation to act as consultants to the Trust. Mr.
Webber had also offered the services of any officers
in his Department to assist in architectural matters.
The Vice President suggested that all Trustees should be
given an opportunity, at some future date, to meet these
two gentlemen and it was left to the President to arrange
this.

summary: The Police Band was confirmed to play in the Vaucluse House grounds on 29 September, but Sergeant Mills requested a change to 6 October because Mr. Maddison wanted the band for another function.
counterparty: Deputy Commissioner of Police; Sergeant Mills; Mr. Maddison
quote:
A letter from the Deputy Commissioner of Police was
read confirming that the Police Band would be pleased
to play in the grounds of Vaucluse House on Sunday after-
noon, 29th September. (Subsequently, Sergeant Mills,
the band conductor, telephoned the writer asking if the
date could be changed to Sunday, 6th October, as Mr.
Maddison wanted them to play at a special function on
the originally proposed date. As we had not undertaken
any advertising, the writer advised Sergeant Mills that
he felt sure that the Trust would be agreeable.)

summary: The Trust had no information about Governor Macquarie's Cookbundoon Tree, so the Secretary/Manager was instructed to seek further information from the Goulburn Historical Society after unsuccessful enquiries elsewhere.
counterparty: Goulburn Historical Society; Mr. Harper; Royal Australian Historical Association; Royal Botanic Gardens
quote:
(b) A letter was tabled from the Goulburn Historical
Society enquiring about some object known as Governor
Macquarie's Cookbundoon Tree which has supposedly been
on display at Vaucluse House in the past. As no member
of the Trust knew anything about this item the Secretary/
Manager was instructed to write to the Society asking
for further information. The latter also advised the
meeting that he had already contacted Mr. Harper of

had discussions with Sergeant Napier of the Vaucluse
Police Station who affirmed that the police would co-
operate, in controlling vandalism and hooliganism in

The Trust agreed that steps should be taken to
instal a telephone in the Ranger's Cottage. It was
also agreed that no action be taken to increase the
lighting in the Park at the present time.

Mr. Snelling drew the Board's attention to the

that a copy should be purchased for the library.

summary: Mrs. Doris Kearney was back at home and continuing to make a satisfactory recovery.

Mrs. Doris Kearney is back at home and is continuing to make a
satisfactory recovery.

summary: Mr. S. Walker of the Nielsen Park staff proceeded on annual leave.

Mr. John Norton was engaged as a Gardener's Labourer to replace

asset: kitchen chimney stack, Manager's flat Esse stove, dormer-window guttering, and east-wall guttering
summary: Maintenance included removing the tall chimney stack from the kitchen's south-east roof and the Esse stove from the Manager's flat, fixing new dormer-window guttering, and restrapping east-wall guttering.
quote:
Maintenance work continues: the tall chimney stack has been removed
from the south-east roof of the kitchen and the Esse stove from the
Manager's flat; new guttering has been fixed to the sides of the dormer
windows of the flat and the guttering on the east wall has been restrapped.

asset: Vaucluse House external walls, woodwork, and white-ant-damaged woodwork
summary: A quotation was requested for repainting external walls and woodwork where required, while careful replacement of white-ant-damaged woodwork had been done and further restoration was proceeding.
quote:
A quotation has been requested for repainting of all external walls
and woodwork where required. Careful replacement of some of the woodwork
in the House, previously damaged by white ants has been done and further
restoration is proceeding.

summary: Pointing of the stable stonework was continuing where necessary.
quote: Pointing of the stonework of the stable is continuing where necessary.

summary: The Service advised proceeding before prices rose; if the Trust covered Stage 1 of the architectural survey from the Special Purposes Account, $6,000 in budget could be transferred to cover installation of the fire-alarm system in the House.
quote:
The writer has discussed this matter with appropriate officers of
the Service and they advised us to proceed with ordering before the price
goes up. If the Trust are prepared to stand the cost of Stage 1 of the
architectural survey from the Special Purposes Account ($2,500, of which
the Friends have already made a contribution of $1,200) then the sum
of $6,000 in our budget can be transferred to cover the cost of the
installation in the House. The Service thoroughly approve of the Con-
tractors and the system which is similar to one currently being installed
at Kosciusko.

summary: No further inventory information was available.
quote: No further information available.

summary: With the pending development of the kitchen, consideration should be given to a subsidiary burglar alarm system to cover that area.
quote:
With the pending development of the kitchen consideration should be
given to a subsidiary burgular alarm system to cover this area.

asset: Vaucluse Park Beach Paddock and foreshore
summary: The Beach Paddock and foreshore were thoroughly cleaned, but the Beach remained a problem because flotsam and jetsam returned within a week of cleaning.
quote:
During the month the Beach Paddock and the foreshore were thoroughly
cleaned, but the Beach is still a great problem as within a week of
cleaning, the flotsam and jetsam is just as bad as it was before the
clean-up.

asset: Vaucluse Park lawns and cypress adjacent to the Tea Rooms

General maintenance work continues and most lawns have received

soil we have lost a very beautiful surface rooted cypress adjacent to
the east end of the Tea Rooms.

quote:
All work apart from a little external touching up of painted sur-
faces has been completed. Mr. and Mrs. J. Kearney entered into occupation
of the cottage on the 23rd August.

summary: Damage to the sea wall had been repaired at a cost of $950, fully recoverable through the Service from Federal Government Storm Damage Funds.
quote:
The damage to the sea wall has been repaired at a cost of $950.
The dislodged pile will be replaced within the next 7 to 10 days depend-
ent on weather conditions at a cost of $1,250. These amounts are fully
recoverable through the Service from Federal Government Storm Damage Funds.

summary: The dislodged pile would be replaced within the next 7 to 10 days, weather permitting, at a cost of $1,250, also fully recoverable through Federal Government Storm Damage Funds.

summary: No firm recommendation had yet been made about the wharf; Mr. Keen advised that old timbers were unsuitable and estimated demolition at $4,000-$6,000 and rebuilding at $30,000-$40,000.

red_flag_reason: The wharf's damaged section was the Trust's responsibility, old timbers were unsuitable for reconstruction, and demolition/rebuilding was estimated at $4,000-$6,000 plus $30,000-$40,000.
quote:
The writer has had further discussions with the Operations Division
of the Service re the future of the wharf, but no firm recommendation
has yet been made. The damaged section, which is our responsibility
has been examined by Mr. Keen, Works Supervisor of Sydney Bridge and
Pile Co. Pty. Ltd., who advises that none of the old timbers are suit-
able for re-construction. He has roughly estimated that to demolish this
section and the old dressing shed would be between $4,000 and $6,000,
and to then rebuild as it was could be between $30,000 and $40,000.
This information has been passed on to Operations Division.

summary: The Maritime Services Board was responsible for the wharf beyond mean low water mark, so the Service favoured returning the west cliff of Shark Bay to nature and asking the Board to remove its section of the wharf.

It has been definitely established that the Maritime Services

therefore, the Service thinking tends to favour returning the west
cliff of Shark Bay to a state of nature and requesting the Maritime
Services Board to remove their section of the wharf.

The Secretary/Manager advised that subsequent to a meeting

Its format had been approved by the Vice-President and

asset: Historic Houses of Australia advertising leaflet
summary: A National Trust letter apologising for a data error in the advertising leaflet for Historic Houses of Australia concerning the building of Vaucluse House was noted.

A letter from the National Trust apologising for a data
error in the advertising leaflet for their forthcoming
publication "Historic Houses of Australia", relative to
the building of Vaucluse House was noted.

asset: Nielsen Park jetty in Shark Bay
summary: The Maritime Services Board's acknowledgment of responsibility for the seaward end of the Shark Bay jetty was received, but discussion of whether to repair or dismantle the seriously damaged structure remained unresolved.
counterparty: Maritime Services Board; Mr. Barrett; Mr. Snelling
red_flag_reason: The jetty had sustained serious winter-gale damage at its landward end, and Trustees disagreed whether it should be repaired and preserved or dismantled.
quote:
A letter from the Maritime Services Board finally acknow-
ledging their responsibility for the seaward end of the
jetty in Shark Bay was received with satisfaction. Consid-
erable discussion then took place regarding the future of
the structure in the light of the serious damage it had
sustained during the winter gales at the landward end. Mr.
Barrett felt that if possible it should be repaired and pres-
erved, whilst Mr. Snelling expressed the view that as the
jetty now served no useful purpose it should be dismantled.
The Secretary/Manager advised that after discussions with

summary: The Trustees discussed demolition or reconstruction of the damaged wharf section, with estimated costs of $12,000 to $15,000 for demolition and a further $60,000 to $80,000 for reconstruction, and deferred the matter pending Mr. Finlay's report on the jetty file.
counterparty: Sydney Bridge and Wharf Co. Pty. Ltd.
red_flag_reason: Damaged wharf section requires costly demolition or reconstruction and original timbers are unusable.
quote:
Service officers he was of the opinion that they favoured
demolition of the structure and the restoration of the
west cliff of Shark Bay to a state of nature. Verbal dis-
cussions with Mr. Keen, Works Supervisor of Sydney Bridge
and Wharf Co. Pty. Ltd., had resulted in him expressing
the opinion that demolition of the damaged section of the
wharf which is our responsibility would cost between
$12,000 and $15,000. Reconstruction would cost between
$60,000 and $80,000 on top of that figure. None of the
original timbers were fit for re-use. After some further
discussion it was agreed that Mr. Finlay's offer to examine
the file on the jetty should be accepted and that he should
report his findings at a subsequent meeting of the Trustees.

summary: The Trust accepted Clive Lucas's commission for Stage 1 of the architectural survey, sought a firm price for proposed plans, and arranged for him to be told about 1966 plans available at the Mitchell Library.
quote:
The President read a letter from Mr. Clive Lucas accept-
ing the Trust's commission to carry out Stage 1 of the
architectural survey on the House. In view of the hourly
rates quoted by Mr. Lucas, Messrs. Finlay, Doyle and Her-
ford all expressed the view that an attempt should be made
to tie Mr. Lucas down to a firm price for the proposed
plans. The President agreed to approach Mr. Lucas in this
matter, but indicated that it may not be necessary for a
complete set of new plans to be prepared as he had been
advised that an excellent set of plans drawn in 1966 was
available at the Mitchell Library. It was left to the
Secretary/Manager to advise Mr. Lucas of the existence
of these plans, which if satisfactory, would enable the
architect to proceed with the more detailed investigations
part of the survey. In this connection it was considered
advisable that he should contact the Chief Archivist of
the Mitchell Library, who, it was understood, had a lot
of information on file about the House going back for
many years.

summary: The Royal Australian Historical Society sought re-possession of the Ranken coach, and the Secretary/Manager was asked to explore replacement exhibits or an exchange for the Cobb and Co. coach.
quote:
A letter from the Royal Australian Historical Society was
read indicating their desire to re-possess the Ranken
coach at present housed in the stables. It is understood
that this will be going to the Old Sydney Town project at
Somersby near Gosford, and it is unlikely that it will
ever be returned for display at our Site. The President
suggested that we should attempt to obtain a suitable coach
or gig to replace the one now being re-possessed and Mr.
Snelling suggested that an approach should be made to the
R.A.H.S. to see if they had a suitable vehicle available.
The president, however, considered that the Cobb and Co.
coach was somewhat out of place in our stables and requested
that the Secretary/Manager see if it could be exchanged for
a more suitable exhibit. The Secretary/Manager undertook
to deal with this matter.

summary: The meeting considered two Sydney Morning Herald letters criticising the Site's administration and agreed to take no action except re-wording the Olola Avenue entrance sign and changing its colour to black and white.
quote:
Copies of two letters appearing in the columns of the
Sydney Morning Herald expressing certain criticism of the
administration of the Site were considered by the Meeting
and it was agreed that no action should be taken apart from

summary: The Trustees unanimously accepted the Executive's recommendation to take Michael Avenell Catering Coy.'s tender, initially granting a six-month restaurant licence while discussions occurred about a future three- to five-year lease.
quote:
On behalf of the Executive the President suggested that
the tender submitted by Michael Avenell Catering Coy.
should be accepted and it was agreed that initially a licence
should be granted for the operation of the restaurant for a
period of six months, during which time discussions could
be carried out between the licensee and the Trustees regard-
ing the format of a lease of the premises of between three
and five years. Mr. Cook proposed, and Mr. Pierce seconded,
that the recommendations of the Executive should be accepted
and the motion was unanimously agreed to by the Trustees.

asset: premises occupied by employees of the Trust
summary: The meeting noted that employee premises licences had been drawn up by Bruce Wilson of the N.P. & W.S. Legal Department and empowered the President to sign for the Trustees.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that these had now been
drawn up by Mr. Bruce Wilson of N.P. & W.S. Legal Department
and the meeting empowered the President to sign on behalf
of the Trustees.

summary: The meeting deferred further action on re-constituting the kitchen area until Clive Lucas could advise on removing plaster from the chimney breast and possible demolition of the wind break, and agreed to restore Gilberthorpe's room for public opening.
red_flag_reason: Kitchen renovation work is deferred pending the architect's recommendations about the chimney breast and wind break.
quote:
The meeting agreed that nothing further could be done
in this matter until advice had been received from Mr. Clive
Lucas, and the Secretary/Manager was requested to get Mr.
Lucas on site as soon as possible in order to obtain his
recommendations regarding the removal of the plaster from
the chimney breast and the possible demolition of the wind
break. The President further suggested that Gilberthorpe's
room be restored for opening to the public and that, after
renovations had been carried out, the Friends of Vaucluse
House should be asked to put forward recommendations regard-
ing the furnishing of this room. The Trustees agreed with
this proposal.

summary: The Trustees viewed the Honours Board provided by the Service and agreed it should be located in a suitable position in the Board Room.
quote:
The Trustees adjourned to the old paint shop to view the
Honours Board provided by the Service and it was agreed
that this should be located in a suitable position in the
Board Room.

summary: After discussions with the Service Finance Department, the meeting agreed to proceed as quickly as possible with installing the fire alarm system in the House, but not yet in the stables.
quote:
It was agreed that, in view of the Secretary/Manager's
discussions with the Finance Department of the Service,
we should proceed with all possible speed to have the
system installed in the House, but not at present in
the stables.

summary: The Secretary/Manager was instructed to press Randall Reed to complete the inventory quickly so insurance premiums could be settled with the Government Insurance Office.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager was instructed to press Mr. Randall
Reed to complete this as soon as possible in order that
our insurance premiums can be settled at an early date
with the Government Insurance Office.

summary: The meeting agreed that the Secretary/Manager should investigate the cost of installing a subsidiary burglar alarm system in the kitchen area.
quote:
It was agreed that the Secretary/Manager should investi-
gate the cost of installing a subsidiary burglar alarm
system in the kitchen area.

summary: The Secretary/Manager reported that Dunlop gave a verbal estimate of $2,500 for the courtyard iron gates, was preparing drawings and a written quotation, and should be introduced to architect Clive Lucas before any order was placed.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that he had held further
discussions on site with Mr. Dunlop who had given a
verbal estimate of $2,500 for manufacture and installation.
Mr. Dunlop was now preparing drawings and a written quot-
ation for this work. It was agreed that, before any order
was given for the manufacture of the gates, Mr. Dunlop
should be introduced to our architect, Mr. Lucas, with
a view to ensuring that the gates were compatible with
the period in which the House was built.

summary: The meeting allocated up to $300 for renovating and repairing the Blue Mountains display to make it more visitor-proof, with further discussion to be had with B.K.S. Displays.
quote:
It was agreed that a sum of up to $300 be allocated for
renovation and repair of this display in order to make
it as "visitor proof" as possible. The Secretary/Manager
undertook to have further discussion in this matter with
B.K.S. Displays.

summary: The Vice President gave notice to discuss parking in the paddocks and rebuilding the gardener's quarters, and the meeting agreed both items should be on the 20 October agenda.
quote:
The Vice President gave notice that he would like to
discuss with other Trustees at the next meeting the question
of the parking of cars in the paddocks and the re-building
of the gardener's quarters at the rear of the stables.
It was agreed that both these items should be included
in the agenda of the Trust meeting of the 20th October.

Automation Symposium being held in connection with an
International Engineering Exhibition at the Sydney
Showground.

quote:
In closing the meeting at 11.25 a.m. the President asked
the members to note that the election of Trust Officers
for the ensuing year would take place at the October
meeting.

summary: The September report noted considerable illness among Vaucluse House staff, with never a full complement on duty during the month.
quote:
There has been a considerable amount of illness amongst Vaucluse
House staff during the month and at any one time there has never been
a full complement of staff on duty.

summary: Mrs. D. Kearney was still on convalescent leave and continuing to make a steady recovery.
quote:
Mrs. D. Kearney is still on convalescent leave and continues to
make a steady recovery.

summary: Mrs. Hall, Mrs. O'Connor, Mrs. Sames and Mr. Kennedy were absent with influenza, fortunately not all at the same time.
counterparty: Mrs. P. Hall, Mrs. J. O'Connor, Mrs. O. Sames and Mr. J. Kennedy
quote:
Mrs. P. Hall, Mrs. J. O'Connor, Mrs. O. Sames and Mr. J. Kennedy
have been absent suffering from influenza, fortunately not all at the
same time.

summary: Mr. V. Verass, gardener's labourer, was discharged because his work performance became unsatisfactory, and no suitable replacement had yet been found.
red_flag_reason: The gardener's labourer was discharged for unsatisfactory work and no suitable replacement had yet been found.
quote:
I discharged Mr. V. Verass, gardener's labourer as his work
performance became quite unsatisfactory. No suitable replacement
has yet been found.

summary: Mr. S. Walker returned from annual leave a week early so Mr. Peter Bloomfield could proceed on his honeymoon immediately after his marriage.
quote:
Mr. S. Walker of Nielsen Park staff returned from his annual
leave a week early in order to allow Mr. Peter Bloomfield to proceed
on his honeymoon immediately following his marriage.

summary: Mr. H. Westbrook attended a tree-surgery course organised at Ku-ring-gai National Park by the Service, and the knowledge acquired was expected to be useful.
quote:
Mr. H. Westbrook attended a tree-surgery course organised at
Ku-ring-gai National Park by the Service, for one week. From subsequent
conversations I have had with him, the course appears to have been most
successful and the knowledge he has acquired should prove to be very
useful to us in the future.

summary: Part-time carpenter Mr. B. Binnie ceased work because of continuing ill health, and Mr. Ivor Wilson was found as an excellent local replacement on a contract basis.
counterparty: Mr. B. Binnie and Mr. Ivor Wilson
quote:
Mr. B. Binnie our part time carpenter has been forced to cease
work due to continuing ill health. I have been fortunate in finding
an excellent replacement in Mr. Ivor Wilson who lives locally. He
will work for the Trust, as required, on a contract basis.

summary: General maintenance continued: unserviceable iron guttering and fall pipes on the east side of the stables were replaced in copper, the western side was repaired where necessary, and masonry pointing was completed.
quote:
General maintenance work continues: the unserviceable iron
guttering and fall pipes on the east side of the stables has been re-
placed in copper and that on the western side has been repaired where
necessary. Pointing of the masonry where required has been completed.

summary: The Ranken Coach was re-possessed by the Royal Australian Historical Society, replacement vehicle steps were being taken, and a Cobb & Co. Royal Mail Coach was temporarily stored in the Fodder Room.
quote:
The Ranken Coach has been re-possessed by the Royal Australian
Historical Society and steps are being taken to find some suitable
vehicle to replace it. At the request of the Director, N.P. & W.S.,
we are temporarily storing a Cobb & Co., Royal Mail Coach in the Fodder
Room. This will eventually be housed permanently at the Hill End Historic
Site which has been restored under the direction of our architect, Mr.
Clive Lucas.

summary: The Trustees' and female staff toilets had been repainted.
quote: The Trustees' and female staff toilets have been repainted.

summary: A B.K.S. Displays representative had examined the Blue Mountains exhibit again, recommendations and a quotation were expected for the next Trust Meeting, and the costume display cabinet had been prepared for models being dressed by Mrs. Kiernan.
quote:
A representative of B.K.S. Displays has examined this exhibit
once again and I hope to have his recommendations and quotation for
presentation at the next Trust Meeting. The costume display cabinet
has been prepared to receive the models being dressed by Mrs. Kiernan.

summary: Mrs. Kiernan and the Secretary/Manager rearranged exhibits in three cases to make room for additional items, including a taffeta padded petticoat, two mid-19th-century samplers, and Margaret Catchpole's ruby and pearl ring.
quote:
Mrs. Kiernan and the writer re-arranged some of the exhibits in
three cases to make room for additional exhibits including a taffeta
padded petticoat and two samplers of the mid 19th century. The beauti-
ful ruby and pearl ring of the convict girl, Margaret Catchpole who
was befriended by Captain Piper and his family has also been placed on
exhibition in one of the display cases.

summary: The de Closey oil painting of the stables and line drawings by Mr. O'Leary were cleaned, restored or framed by Academy Arts Galleries of Rose Bay, and would be available for Trustees to examine.
quote:
The de Closey oil painting of the stables which I found some time
ago in the Archives has been cleaned, restored and framed. The line
drawings by Mr. O'Leary of Sir Henry Brown-Hayes ancestral home "Mount
Vernon" and of the church in which his remains are interred at Cork
in Eire have also been framed. This work has been meticulously done
by Academy Arts Galleries of Rose Bay to whom I think we could safely
entrust any other work of this type. The pictures will be available
for examination by Trustees on Sunday next.

summary: Wormald Electrics had commenced installation of the fire alarm system, with completion hoped for before the end of October.
quote:
Wormald Electrics have commenced installation and it is hoped that
completion will be effected before the end of October.

summary: The Secretary/Manager had seen Randall Reed and introduced him to the President; Reed promised to complete the inventory project in time for the 20 October 1974 Board Meeting.
quote:
I have seen Mr. Randall Reed and also introduced him to the Presi-
dent. He has promised to have this project completed in time for the
Board Meeting on the 20th October, 1974.

summary: Hodgson & Lee withdrew from the burglar alarm installation business and returned the division to Alert Alarms; Mr. Ryan assured efficient maintenance and was preparing a quotation for a subsidiary kitchen-area system.
quote:
Hodgson & Lee have withdrawn from the burglar alarm installation
business and have returned this division to the care of Alert Alarms
from whom they acquired it some fourteen years ago. The Managing
Director, Mr. Ryan has been to see me and assured me of efficient
maintenance of our existing system and is preparing a quotation for
a subsidiary system for the kitchen area.

summary: Clive Lucas had made a preliminary investigation of the House, would visit the Mitchell Library to examine documents and plans, and hoped to advise the Trust about the kitchen and main staircase soon.
quote:
Mr. Clive Lucas has made a preliminary investigation of the House
and has been furnished with relevant information the writer has collected
about the House during the past twelve months. He will also visit the
Mitchell Library to examine documents and plans as requested by the
President. Mr. Lucas hopes to give the Trust his advice relative to
the kitchen and the main staircase in the near future.

summary: The House and grounds were used as background for ABC-TV's comedy film 'Flash Nick from Jindivick', and the Secretary/Manager negotiated a $150 donation to Trust funds.
quote:
The House and grounds have been used as background for a new
comedy film being made about bushrangers in the early days entitled,
"Flash Nick from Jindivick". The writer has negotiated a donation
to Trust funds of $150.00.

summary: Despite staff shortages, much work was done in the grounds; the lawns were showing recovery from winter damage and regular mowing was in operation.
quote:
Despite staff shortages much work has been done in the grounds,
the lawns are showing signs of recovery from the damage sustained during
the winter and regular mowing is now in operation.

summary: Because contractors failed to install the new pile, the pool could not open as planned on 5 October; the report said weather likely prevented revenue loss and may have saved $200 in wages, and the pool opened on 12 October 1974.
red_flag_reason: Contractors failed to install the new pile, delaying opening of the pool as planned.
quote: Due to the failure of the contractors to install the new pile it

summary: No problems were encountered in supervising Clark Island.
quote: No problems were encountered in supervising Clark Island.

summary: The September financial report stated total income including admissions, sales and rents was $5,715.24, of which $3,184.56 was General Revenue due to N.P. & W.S. and $2,530.68 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
This has been an exceptionally good month for the time of the year
with admissions up to "tourist season" standards. Total income inclusive
of admissions, sales, rents, etc. was $5,715.24 of which General Revenue
due to N.P. & W.S. was $3,184. 56 whilst $2,530.68 was credited to the
Special Purposes Account.

summary: Current financial year allocations were not yet available, so the report said allocations were being kept as near as possible to the 1973/74 allocations.
quote:
Allocations are not yet to hand for the current financial year. I
am therefore, keeping as near as possible to the allocations for 1973/74.
