Messrs. Yelland, Finlay and Barrett were unanimously re-elected as President, Vice-President and Treasurer respectively for the ensuing year.
quote:
Messrs. Yelland, Finlay and Barrett were unanimously re-
elected to fill the positions of President, Vice-President
and Treasurer respectively for the ensuing year.

summary: The draft agreement for the Longhurst drawings between the Trust, Mr. Longhurst and Artstaff Creative Services had been forwarded to the N.P. & W.S. Legal Department, but official documents were not yet available.
counterparty: Mr. Longhurst and Artstaff Creative Services
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that the draft agreement
between the Trust, Mr. Longhurst and Artstaff Creative
Services had been forwarded to the Legal Department of
N.P. & W.S. for the drawing up of the official documents.
These were not yet to hand.

summary: The Service agreed to make the damaged Nielsen Park jetty structure safe, but its future depended on Commonwealth storm damage funds; the shoreward end had been boarded up, a keep-off notice erected, and demolition of part of the old dressing shed was under way.
red_flag_reason: The damaged jetty structure's future depends on Commonwealth storm damage funds, and the public has been advised it is unsafe.
quote:
The President advised that as a result of discussions
with the Director, when he visited the House on the
16th October, 1974, it had been agreed that the Service
would undertake to render the damaged structure safe, but
its future was dependent on storm damage funds being made
available by the Commonwealth Government. The Vice-Pres-
ident then briefly re-viewed the history of the jetty
during the past few years and felt that, pending demolition
of the structure, the Trust could do no more than had
been done in advising the public that it was unsafe.
The Secretary/Manager confirmed that the shoreward end
of the jetty had been boarded up and a "Keep-off" notice
had been erected. The Nielsen Park staff were demol-
ishing as much of the old dressing shed alongside the
jetty as was required to render it safe.

summary: The President approved paintings and prints offered by Miss Myles in exchange for works in the House that had to be returned, and the Secretary/Manager was asked to arrange the exchange.
quote:
He had visited the Library and approved the paintings
and prints offered by Miss Myles, the Picture Librarian,
in exchange for those presently in the House which had
to be returned. The Secretary/Manager was requested
to make the necessary detailed arrangements with Miss
Myles for the exchange.

summary: The President saw 1966 House plans by Brogan, Lynch and Nicholas, but they could not be traced and copyright may make copies difficult for Clive Lucas; the Chief Archivist promised to help if possible.
red_flag_reason: The 1966 House plans could not be traced and copyright may make copies difficult to obtain for Clive Lucas.
quote:
The President also advised that he had sighted the plans
made in 1966 by Messrs. Brogan, Lynch and Nicholas when
they were students in the School of Architecture at
The University of New South Wales. Unfortunately these
three gentlemen could not now be traced and, as they held
the copyright of the plans, there might be some difficulty
in having copies made available for the use of Mr. Clive
Lucas. However, the Chief Archivist had promised to
help if at all possible.

summary: The Ranken Coach had been collected for transfer to the Old Sydney Town Project; the Trust could not afford Ellenden's Town Carriage, but Mr. Cook was authorised to offer free storage if there was no immediate purchaser, and the Trust would seek a gig and eventually replace the Cobb & Co. Coach.
counterparty: Royal Australian Historical Society and Ellenden's
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that this had now been
collected on behalf of the Royal Australian Historical
Society for transfer to the Old Sydney Town Project at
Somersby. It was agreed that we could not afford to
purchase the Town Carriage on offer from Ellenden's,
but if there was no immediate purchaser for this vehicle
Mr. Cook was authorised to offer free storage pending a
sale being made. It was further agreed that we should
attempt to locate a gig for display in the Coach House
and that eventually the Cobb & Co. Coach should be
replaced by a more appropriate exhibit.

summary: Because the restaurant licence was not available before Mrs. McCole's lease ended, Michael Avenell Catering Company agreed to operate on a weekly tenancy basis under a letter of intent; the Trust agreed to meet part of glazing costs and future toilet costs, while Mr. Herford's disagreement was recorded.
red_flag_reason: The restaurant licence was delayed by Legal Department workload, and Mr. Herford disagreed with the Trust's glazing and toilet-cost concessions.
quote:
Due to pressure of work in the Legal Department of the
N.P. & W.S., the Licence for the Restaurant was not avail-
able for signature prior to the termination of the former
lease held by Mrs. McCole. However, Michael Avenell
Catering Company had agreed to operate the restaurant on
a weekly tenancy basis on receipt of a letter of intent
to issue the licence. This letter, a copy of which was
produced at the meeting, had been drafted by Mr. Bruce
Wilson of the Legal Department of the Service and signed
on behalf of the Trust by the Secretary/Manager. It was
further agreed that the Trust would meet part of the
cost of completing the glazing of the restaurant and,
should a liquor licence be granted at a later date, the
Trust would cover the cost of erecting the necessary
toilet facilities, but these would be entirely to the
Trust's own specifications. Mr. Herford had expressed
his disagreement with these concessions and asked that
this should be recorded. The Vice-President once again stressed
that when the time came to apply for a liquor licence, Mr.
Wilson should seek advice from Mr. K. Smithers.

summary: Clive Lucas asked that no repairs be made to the main staircase supporting walls, no plaster stripped from the kitchen chimney breast, and no replacement of the courtyard wooden slatted gates until he had clarified and investigated the projects; the Trust agreed to follow his advice.
red_flag_reason: Repairs to supporting walls, plaster stripping and courtyard gate replacement were deferred pending the architect's clarification and investigations.
quote:
The President read a letter which he had received from
Mr. Clive Lucas relating to his initial inspection of
the House in which he requested that no action be taken
regarding repairs to the supporting walls of the main
staircase or the stripping of the plaster from the chimney
breast in the kitchen until he had clarified his thoughts
on both projects. He further suggested that no action
be taken to replace the wooden slatted gates to the court-
yard until he had carried out further investigations and
research. The Trust agreed to take the architect's advice.

summary: Longhurst offered the eight original drawings to the Trust for $800, but because they could not be reproduced without the Trust's sanction the meeting felt there was no point purchasing them at that price and asked the Secretary/Manager to advise him.
quote:
A letter from the artist was read in which he offered
the eight original drawings to the Trust for $800.00.
As the drawings could not be reproduced without the
Trust's sanction, it was felt that there was no point
in purchasing the originals at the price quoted. The
Secretary/Manager was requested to advise Mr. Longhurst
accordingly.

summary: The Bondi Surf Lifesaving Club requested use of the Nielsen Park netted swimming area for its February/March annual championships, and the meeting agreed to offer the facilities again.
quote:
A letter was received from the Club requesting the use
of the Nielsen Park netted swimming area for their
annual championships in February/March. It was agreed
that we would once again offer them our facilities.

summary: The meeting agreed not to restrict parking on the West Paddock for the time being, but to try to protect vulnerable trees; after discussion of ropes, stumps and boulders, advice was to be sought from the Service.
red_flag_reason: Car parking may damage grass and tree roots, and practical protection methods were uncertain.
quote:
The Vice-President reviewed the position regarding this
concession with special reference to the possible damage
to the grass and the root formation of certain trees.
After considerable discussion it was agreed that for the
time being parking on the West Paddock should not be
restricted, but that an attempt be made to protect any
particularly vulnerable trees. Mr. Herford suggested
that an area around the trees could be roped off. The
Secretary/Manager pointed out that in the centre of a
boating community this was not a practical proposition
as the ropes would disappear, just as the chains do,
which are used in certain areas of the park. Mr. Doyle
suggested that tree stumps could be sunk into the ground
to prevent cars parking under trees, and the President
thought that large boulders could be used. The Secretary/
manager considered that either of these methods would
make mowing difficult and suggested that advice should
be sought from the Service. It was agreed that this
should be done.

summary: All Trustees agreed the Gardeners' Compound was an eyesore, especially on the east side of the stable; Mr. Barrett would examine it and propose an improvement scheme, including use of the glasshouse, at the next meeting.
quote:
All Trustees agreed that this essential area was some-
what of an eyesore, especially on the east side of the
stable. Mr. Barrett offered to examine this area and
put forward a scheme for improvement at the next meeting.
He would also see what could be done to improve the
utilisation of the glasshouse.

summary: The Director and Mr. Beaman indicated consideration of a re-design of the Blue Mountains exhibit; the Secretary/Manager expected a B.K.S. Displays quotation for strengthening the present exhibit but would liaise with Mr. Beaman before proceeding.
quote:
The President advised that during a recent visit to
the House by the Director and Mr. Beaman, Head of the
Interpretations Division of the Service he had indicated
that consideration would be given to a re-design of this
exhibit. The Secretary/Manager advised that he was ex-
pecting a quotation from B.K.S. Displays for the strength-
ening of the present exhibit, but in view of Mr. Beaman's
remarks he would liaise with him regarding the work be-
fore putting it in hand.

summary: The meeting agreed to rationalise Trust committees into a House Committee, a Grounds Committee, and an Insurance, Legal Matters and Public Relations Committee, with Mr. Snelling requested to take responsibility for the museum area including the Blue Mountains Exhibition.
quote:
were looked after by Mr. Finlay, matters concerning
insurance were looked after by Mr. Doyle, and Mr. Herford
and Mr. Cook were consulted in anything concerning the
contents of the House. It was therefore agreed that this
position should be rationalised and initially there should
be three committees as follows: HOUSE COMMITTEE, Messrs.
Herford and Cook; GROUNDS COMMITTEE, Messrs. Barrett and
Pierce; INSURANCE, LEGAL MATTERS AND PUBLIC RELATIONS,
Messrs. Finlay and Doyle, and as Mr. Snelling, since his
retirement, had offered at least half a day per week
to assist with the House, it was decided that he should
be requested to assume responsibility for the develop-
ment of the museum area including the Blue Mountains
Exhibition. The President would be ex-officio member
of all committees.

summary: The Trust agreed to the Public Service Board-approved seasonal worker rates of pay and to increase the float for paying these workers from $200 to $250.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager presented the rates of pay as
approved by the Public Service Board and these were
agreed to by the Trust. They also agreed to the in-
crease of the float to pay these workers, from $200 to
$250.

summary: The Trustees noted with regret that carpenter Bruce Binnie had been advised by his doctor to give up work, and agreed to send him a letter of appreciation for his valuable services.
quote:
The Trustees noted with regret that our carpenter Mr.
Bruce Binnie had been advised by his doctor to give up
work. It was agreed that a letter of appreciation should
be sent to Mr. Binnie regarding his valuable services to
the Trust over many years.

summary: The inventory completed by Randall Reed was noted with satisfaction, and the Secretary/Manager was asked to provide a copy for Mr. Doyle's insurance work on the House contents.
quote:
The production, at the meeting, of the inventory com-
pleted by Mr. Randall Reed was noted with satisfaction
and the Secretary/Manager was requested to have a copy
made for the use of Mr. Doyle, who is dealing with the
matter of insurance on the contents of the House.

summary: The financial report was accepted and Recoup Summaries 14 to 21 were formally confirmed by the Board after being passed for payment and endorsed by the National Parks and Wildlife Service.
quote:
The financial report was accepted and Recoup Summaries
Nos. 14-21 were tabled. As they had already been passed
for payment and endorsed by the National Parks and Wild-
life Service they were formally confirmed by the Board.

summary: The Friends of Vaucluse House wished to hold a garden party during February/March 1975, and the Trust approved and wished them success.
quote:
Mr. Doyle advised that it was the wish of the Friends
to hold a garden party at some date to be determined
during February/March, 1975. The Trust approved and
wished the Friends every success in this venture.

summary: The President said he had asked the Friends to consider re-furnishing Gilberthorpe's Room in the style of a senior servant of the 1840/50 period.
quote:
The President advised the meeting that he had asked the
Friends to give consideration to the re-furnishing of
this room in the style of that of a senior servant of
the 1840/50 period.

summary: The meeting agreed that action should be taken to establish or disprove the authenticity of the Pompeian tiles, with Mr. Cook and the Secretary/Manager to look into it.
quote:
It was agreed that some action should be taken to
establish or disprove the authenticity of these tiles
and Mr. Cook in conjunction with the Secretary/Manager
would look into this matter.

summary: Mr. Herford tabled correspondence about the Royal Pavilion, and the Secretary/Manager was instructed to write to Keeper J.M.A. Dinkel seeking expert advice on furnishing the kitchen and displaying the Batterie de cuisine.
quote:
Mr. Herford tabled copies of correspondence between
the Keeper of the Royal Pavilion, Brighton, England and one
of his friends, Mr. LeRoy-Lewis. The Secretary/Manager
was instructed to write to the Keeper of the Royal
Pavilion, Mr. J.M.A. Dinkel, seeking his expert advice

summary: The final location of the Honours Board was to be decided later, with possible sites in the Boardroom or the old paint shop in the stables when it became an Archives and Historians' Room.
quote:
It was agreed that the final location of this board
should be decided at a later date. There were two
possible sites, firstly, in the Boardroom and secondly,
in the old paint shop in the stables when it is turned into
an Archives and Historians' Room.

summary: The President proposed that as many Trustees as possible meet new consultants Professor Ward and Mr. Webber, and the meeting agreed to arrange a Boardroom luncheon for 15 November at 12.30 p.m.
quote:
The President suggested that he felt it advisable for
as many members of the Trust as possible to meet our
new consultants, Professor Ward and Mr. Webber and
it was agreed that a luncheon should be arranged for
this purpose in the Boardroom for 15th November at
12.30 p.m. The Trustees were asked to advise the
Secretary/Manager if they intended to be present and
he was to make the necessary arrangements with Michael
Avenell Catering Coy.

summary: The President reported that the Service might take over control of Nielsen Park, and the Trustees expressed satisfaction with the proposal.
quote:
(1) The possibility of the Service taking over the
control of Nielsen Park. The Trustees expressed sat-
isfaction with this proposal.

summary: The President proposed transferring the large sideboard from the Guests' Diningroom to Greycliffe House for exhibition, and the Trustees approved the transfer.
quote:
(2) The President referred to the very large sideboard
currently located in the Guests' Diningroom which most
Trustees have always considered too big and overpowering
for this area. We already had in store a most excellent,
but smaller sideboard to take its place and he asked if
the Trustees would be agreeable, at the proper time, for
the big sideboard to be transferred for exhibition on
the ground floor of Greycliffe House, as it was the
intention of the Service to furnish at least two rooms
with furniture of the mid-nineteenth century period.
The Trustees gave their approval of this transfer.

summary: The Director was investigating Mrs. Phillip Simpson's criticism of the Trustees' administration in a letter to the Minister; the President said the Trust had taken proper action on the issues, but no evidence linked Mrs. Simpson to the Friends, and he would write to her personally.
red_flag_reason: A letter to the Minister criticised the Trustees' administration on several issues, including the Blue Mountains Exhibition, advisory experts, architects' supervision and cataloguing.
quote:
(3) The President reported that the Director was also
investigating a criticism of the Trustees' administration,
recently made in a letter from Mrs. Phillip Simpson to
the Minister. Four issues had been raised in this letter;
The Crossing of the Blue Mountains Exhibition, an advis-
ory committee of experts, architects' supervision of
renovations and the cataloguing of the contents of the
House.

summary: Mr. Cook presented the House with an early 19th-century candle-maker, and it was agreed that it should be exhibited in an appropriate place in the kitchen area.
quote:
Mr. Cook presented the House with an early 19th century
candle-maker and it was agreed that this should be
exhibited in some appropriate place in the kitchen area.

summary: The President presented to the Trust a 19th-century leather-bound prayer book and hymnal.
quote:
The President then presented to the Trust a 19th
century prayer book and hymnal bound in leather and

summary: A leather reticule that had belonged to an aunt was agreed to be put on display, probably in the costume room.
quote:
contained in a leather reticule which had belonged to
his aunt, and it was agreed that it should be put on display,
probably in the costume room.

summary: The Service had money available to begin demolition of the damaged Nielsen Park jetty section, with officers to proceed after advising interested parties.
red_flag_reason: Damaged jetty section requires demolition and the work is still being coordinated with other parties.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that the Service had the money
available to commence demolition of the damaged section of
the jetty. Mr. Johnstone indicated that his officers in
the Operations Division had the matter in hand, and would
proceed with the work after advising other interested
parties, e.g. Maritime Services Board, Woollahra Council, etc.

summary: Mr. Lucas decided to proceed with accurate measured plans and drawings, but had not yet advised on the kitchen chimney breast and draught screen.
red_flag_reason: The architect had not given further advice on the kitchen chimney breast and draught screen, leaving the decision pending.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that Mr. Lucas did not con-
sider the copy drawings from the Mitchell Library were
very accurate and felt that he must, as originally planned,
proceed with the preparation of accurate, measured plans
and drawings.

summary: The trustees agreed that the public could park free of charge on the western paddock for the time being.
quote:
It was agreed that for the time being the public would be
permitted to park free of charge on the western paddock.

asset: Blue Mountains exhibition area in the stables
summary: After B.K.S. Displays completed strengthening of the Blue Mountains display, the trustees agreed Mr. Snelling should plan the whole exhibition area in the stables.
quote:
As strengthening of the display had been completed by
BKS Displays it was agreed that Mr. Snelling should proceed
with the planning of the whole exhibition area in the stables.

summary: The trustees agreed that a stored sideboard should eventually be installed in the Guests' Diningroom and an over-large sideboard transferred to Greycliffe House when convenient.
quote:
It was further agreed that the sideboard currently stored
in this area should eventually be installed in the Guests'
Diningroom and that the over-large sideboard presently in
that room be transferred to Greycliffe House when conven-
ient to the Service. Mr. Johnstone thanked the Trustees
for their very generous offer of this sideboard for dis-
play in the ground floor section of Greycliffe House when
it eventually opens to the public.

summary: The trustees concurred with the President's handling of Mrs. Simpson's criticism, agreed to drop the correspondence, and asked for her 1972 report to be copied to House Committee members.
red_flag_reason: Mrs. Simpson's criticism of trustees' administration had generated correspondence with the Minister and required a decision to drop the matter.
quote:
The President again referred to the letter written by Mrs.
Simpson to the Minister and then read a letter which he
had written to her after discussing this matter at the
last meeting with the Trustees. He then read the reply
which he had received from Mrs. Simpson. The Trustees
concurred unanimously with the action taken by the President
and further agreed that no useful purpose would be served
by prolonging the correspondence and that therefore, the
matter should be dropped. It was however agreed that the
Secretary/Manager should provide the members of the House
Committee with a copy of Mrs. Simpson's original report
to the Trustees written in 1972.

summary: The trustees approved the Director's request to hold the N.P. & W.S. Advisory Committee annual meeting at the House on 14 December 1974 with a barbeque afterwards.
quote:
A letter from the Director was read, formally requesting
permission to hold the Annual Meeting of the N.P. & W.S.
Advisory Committee, of which he is chairman, on Saturday after-
noon, December 14, 1974 at the House with a barbeque to follow
for the members of the committee and their families. The
Trust gave their hearty approval to this request. It was
agreed that the details should be worked out between the
Secretary/Manager and the appropriate officers of the
Service.

summary: The trustees accepted the Brody Knight catering bill despite criticism, with trustees and counsellor paying for themselves and guests' meals and table and chair hire paid from the entertaining allocation.
red_flag_reason: Trustees were critical of the meal and service but had no alternative but to accept the bill as rendered.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager tabled a bill which had been rendered
by the Brody Knight Catering Service. All Trustees were
critical of the quality of the meal and the service provided,
but agreed that there was no alternative but to accept the
bill as rendered. It was agreed that all Trustees and the
Counsellor would personally pay for their wives and them-
selves, but that the guests' meals and the hire of the
tables and chairs would be paid from the special allocation
for entertaining. The Secretary/Manager was requested to
submit a bill to each Trustee and Counsellor.

summary: The trustees agreed to publicise the Police Band concert on 22 December 1974 in the Wentworth Courier and This Week in Sydney.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager tabled a letter he had received from
the Assistant Commissioner advising that permission had
been given for the Police Band to play on the lawns of
Vaucluse House on Sunday, 22nd December, 1974. It was
agreed that this concert should be publicised by advertis-
ing in the "Wentworth Courier" and the weekly magazine,
"This Week in Sydney".

summary: After receiving a conciliatory letter from Australian Bridge and Wharf about the Nielsen Pool pile, the trustees decided to continue withholding payment and arrange a meeting between company executives, Mr. Barrett and the Secretary/Manager.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.
red_flag_reason: The pile installation was unsatisfactory and payment was being withheld pending resolution.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager read a letter from the Managing
Director of the Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.
(formerly Sydney Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd.) which was a
reply to his own letter expressing doubts as to the effic-
iency of the pile which had been driven in at the Nielsen
Pool. It was agreed that the letter from the Australian
Bridge and Wharf Pty. Ltd. was most conciliatory, but in the
circumstances a number of Trustees felt that we should
continue to withhold payment. Mr. Finlay confirmed that

summary: The trustees welcomed Mr. Peter Jones's offer to clean and look after the South Paddock pool free of charge and asked the Secretary/Manager to discuss it with him.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager tabled a letter which he had received
from a young man, Mr. Peter Jones, who lives locally ex-
pressing concern about the state of the pool at the south
end of the south paddock. Mr. Jones then went on to offer
his services entirely free of charge to generally clean up
this area and look after it when this is done. The Trustees
agreed that it was a welcome experience to find someone
willing to do a good service without financial reward and
it was unanimously agreed that the Secretary/Manager should
ask Mr. Jones to call upon him and discuss the matter in
greater detail.

summary: The trustees agreed that the Secretary/Manager should formally reply agreeing to hand over Nielsen Park at a date to be decided by the Director, while mentioning matters raised in discussion.
quote:
The President read the letter which had been received from
Mr. Johnstone regarding the formation of the Sydney Harbour
National Park and the subsequent vesting of the control of
Nielsen Park in the Director. After the reading of the letter
Mr. Johnstone answered queries put to him by a number of
Trustees and it was then agreed that the Secretary/Manager
should formally reply agreeing to the hand over of Nielsen
Park at a date to be decided by the Director, but that certain
matters which had arisen during discussions should be mentioned
in this reply. (A copy of the Trust's letter is attached
for the information of Trustees.)

summary: Despite local opposition, the trustees resolved to advise the Tea Rooms lessees to apply for the liquor licence and recommended engaging Mr. Ken Smithers for the hearing.
counterparty: Woollahra Council; Vaucluse House Protection Campaign; local residents
red_flag_reason: Local residents, the Vaucluse Progress Association, a protection campaign, Woollahra Council, and others opposed the proposed wine licence.
quote:
The Trustees received with satisfaction the letter from The
Minister of Lands signifying his approval for the Trustees
to support an application by the Lessee of the Tea Rooms
for a licence to serve wines and beer with a mid-day meal.
This application to be made in the normal manner through the
Licensing Court.

summary: The trustees agreed that most paintings and prints in the House should eventually be Trust property so pictures and frames are complementary and of the correct period.
quote:
As mentioned in the Secretary/Manager's report the exchange
of paintings and prints had taken place. He also reported
that with the co-operation of Mr. Nielsen, the new picture
restorer of the Mitchell Library, he had been able to trace
the paintings taken away some three or four years ago for
restoration and it was hoped that these would be available
for re-hanging in the House in the near future. After some
further discussion the Trustees agreed that it was desirable
that eventually most of the paintings and prints in the House
should be Trust property, thus ensuring that all pictures
and frames were complementary to the House and of the correct
period.

summary: The trustees viewed the $150 sulky in the coach-house and approved the purchase, noting it would be worth at least $1,000 after restoration.
quote:
The President reported the purchase of a sulky at a price of
$150. Some restoration is required but basically the vehicle
is in sound condition and very similar to the type actually
used by W.C. Wentworth. The Trustees viewed the sulky in
the coach-house and expressed their approval of the purchase
as after restoration it would be worth at least $1,000.

summary: Mr. Cook reported that the Ellenden Coach, for which the Trust had offered free storage, would probably be returned to England because it would fetch a higher price there.
quote:
(ii) Mr. Cook reported that the Ellenden Coach, for which
we had offered free storage, would probably be returned to
England as it would fetch a higher price there than in Australia.

summary: Mr. Cook recommended considering purchase of the Davenport Desk for no more than $300, and the Trust left it to the Secretary/Manager to see whether Mrs. Couzens would accept that offer.
quote:
(iii) Mr. Cook also reported that he had examined the Daven-
port Desk offered by Mrs. Couzens of Dee Why and suggested
that it would be a good acquisition and we should consider
purchasing it for a sum not exceeding $300. The Trust concurred
and left it to the Secretary/Manager to see if Mrs. Couzens
would accept this offer.

asset: kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen
summary: Mr. Herford pressed for a definite recommendation from Mr. Lucas on the kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen, and the Secretary/Manager undertook to apply pressure.
red_flag_reason: The architect had not given a definite recommendation for the kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and draught screen.
quote:
(iv) Insofar as re-constitution of the kitchen is concerned
Mr. Herford again stressed that pressure should be brought
to bear on Mr. Lucas, architect, to give a definite recommen-
dation on what should be done with the fireplace, chimney breast
and draught screen. The Secretary/Manager undertook to apply
as much pressure as possible.

summary: The trustees agreed that a pine dresser for the kitchen should be sought.
quote:
It was agreed that a pine dresser for the kitchen should be
sought.

summary: The Grounds Committee reported improvements to the greenhouse and proposed improvements to the gardeners' compound; the Trust approved the scheme in principle and sought Mr. Lucas's opinion.
quote:
Mr. Barrett reported that a sprinkler system and a good
selection of plants had been installed in the greenhouse
giving it a much improved appearance. He then presented a
sketch made by the Secretary/Manager of the Committee's pro-
posals for improving the appearance of the gardeners' com-
pound. In principle the Trust approved of the scheme, but
suggested that the opinion of the architect, Mr. Clive Lucas
be sought. The Secretary/Manager undertook to contact Mr. Lucas.

summary: Mr. Doyle said revised insurance cover had not yet been finalised but would be dealt with as soon as possible, and the Trust agreed to proceed with a press-release public-relations suggestion.
red_flag_reason: Revised insurance cover had not been finalised because of pressures on Mr. Doyle's time.
quote:
Mr. Doyle said that many pressures on his time particularly
with regard to the proposed licence for the Tea Rooms had pre-
vented him finalising revised insurance cover, but he would
be dealing with this as soon as possible. Insofar as P.R.
was concerned he believed that a press release about four
times a year to the local papers relating to Trust activities
would be valuable in addition to any historical articles
submitted by Trustees. The Trust agreed that the committee
should proceed with this suggestion.

summary: The October financial report recorded total income of $7,103.34, including $4,637.57 as general revenue due to N.P. & W.S. and $2,465.77 credited to the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
This has been another good month for admissions to the House and
some revenue is starting to come in from Nielsen Pool, although the air
and water temperatures are not yet high enough to draw large crowds of
bathers. Total income inclusive of admissions, sales, rents etc was:
$7,103.34 of which General Revenue due to N.P. & W.S. was $4,637.57 and
$2,465.77 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.

summary: The November financial report recorded total income of $7,164.46, including $5,219.29 as general revenue due to N.P. & W.S. and $1,945.17 credited to the Special Purposes Account.
red_flag_reason: Basic allocations were severely curtailed and maintenance and development work had to be met from the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
Total income inclusive of admissions, sales, .rents, etc. was
$7,164.46 of which General Revenue due to the N.P. & W.S. was $5,219.29
whilst $1,945.17 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.

summary: The Treasurer and Secretary/Manager were carefully checking Special Purposes commitments because allocations were curtailed, leaving $9,266.07 available subject to possible adjustment.
red_flag_reason: Available Special Purposes funds were subject to a possible Finance Division adjustment for expenditure over $3,500 before allocations were known.
quote:
As our basic allocations have been severely curtailed for the current
financial year and as all maintenance and development work expenses have
now to be met from the Special Purposes Account the Treasurer and the
writer are keeping a very careful check on all Special Purposes Account
commitments. Nevertheless, the moneys available from the Special Purposes
Account should enable the Trust to carry on with most of its projects
during the remainder of the current financial year.

summary: The new fire alarm system was commissioned on 14 November and was operating satisfactorily, pending connection to the nearest fire station when G.P.O. made a line available.
quote:
(i) The new fire alarm system was finally commissioned on the 14th November
and appears to be operating satisfactorily. It will be connected to the
nearest fire station as soon as the G.P.O. make a line available.

summary: Two fine 19th century vases loaned by Mrs. Burfitt were collected and put on display in the Guests' Diningroom.
quote:
(ii) Two fine 19th century vases have been loaned to the House by a Mrs.
Burfitt of Elizabeth Bay. The writer collected them and they are now on
display in the Guests' Diningroom.

asset: Conrad Martens watercolour of Sydney Harbour from Vaucluse
summary: Mr. Nielsen completed restoration of the Conrad Martens watercolour, which was returned to its old position in the Morning Room.
quote:
(iii) Mr. Nielsen has made a very fine job of the restoration of the Conrad
Martens watercolour of "Sydney Harbour from Vaucluse" and it is now back
in its old position in the Morning Room.

asset: French clock with Sevres porcelain panels
summary: The French clock with Sevres porcelain panels was successfully repaired, was keeping good time, and was back in the Guests' Diningroom.
quote:
(iv) The French clock with Sevres porcelain panels has been successfully
repaired and is keeping good time. It is back in position in the Guests'
Diningroom.

asset: walls cut for fire alarm cables
summary: Re-plastering of walls that had been cut to take fire alarm cables was carried out.
quote:
(v) Re-plastering of walls, cut into to take the fire alarm cables, has
been carried out.

summary: On 21 November the appointed trustees, attended by the Secretary/Manager, met the deputation from the Vaucluse House Protection Campaign.
quote:
(vi) On the 21st November the appointed Trustees attended by the writer
met the deputation from the so-called "Vaucluse House Protection Campaign".

summary: The Service agreement regarding the Longhurst Drawings was now available and would be tabled at the 15 December Trust Meeting before execution.
quote:
(vii) The Service prepared agreement regarding the "Longhurst Drawings" is
now to hand and will be tabled at the Trust Meeting on the 15th December.
If approved the writer will proceed with execution.

asset: kitchen fireplace and wind-break; gardeners' compound
summary: Further site discussions with Mr. Clive Lucas did not produce a firm recommendation on the kitchen fireplace and wind-break; he advised leaving the gardeners' compound as it was and screening with bushes or creeper.
red_flag_reason: Mr. Lucas remained unwilling to make a firm recommendation about the kitchen fireplace and wind-break.
quote:
(viii) As requested at the last meeting the writer has had further discussions
on site with Mr. Clive Lucas, but he is still unwilling to make any firm
recommendation regarding the kitchen fireplace and wind-break. Also, in
regard to the gardeners' compound, he considers that it should be left as
it is, as a corrugated iron structure is not out of keeping with the period
of the House. Any desired "screening" of the area should be done with bushes,
creeper, etc.

asset: Blue Mountains exhibition and adjoining rooms
summary: Mr. Snelling had been visiting the House weekly to plan the Blue Mountains exhibition area and examine items likely to be suitable for exhibition.
quote:
Mr. Snelling has visited the House each week since the last meeting
and is actively planning the area and examining all items likely to be
suitable for exhibition. He will be reporting at the next meeting.

summary: The Secretary/Manager collected two models from Mrs. Kiernan and helped install them in the case in the exhibition rooms.
quote:
The writer has collected the two mod els from Mrs. Kiernan and assisted
her to instal them in the case in the exhibition rooms.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig overhanging the Tea Rooms
summary: The large Moreton Bay Fig overhanging the Tea Rooms was a cause of great concern, and the President and Treasurer agreed to consult a tree surgeon about having it lopped.
red_flag_reason: The large Moreton Bay Fig overhanging the Tea Rooms was a cause of great concern and required specialist attention.
quote:
The lawns have almost recovered from the disastrous attack last winter
by web moth and army beetles. High winds have once again brought down a
number of branches from various trees. The large Moreton Bay Fig over-
hanging the Tea Rooms is a cause of great concern and the President and the

asset: roof over the kitchen area of the Tea Rooms
summary: Repairs to a leaking roof over the kitchen area of the Tea Rooms were carried out.
quote:
Repairs to a leaking roof over the kitchen area of the Tea Rooms
have been carried out.

summary: The Secretary/Manager interviewed Mr. Peter Jones about cleaning the South Paddock pond and considered his offer should be accepted, with assistance from Mr. John Kearney.
counterparty: Mr. Peter Jones of Hopetoun Avenue
quote:
The writer has interviewed Mr. Peter Jones of Hopetoun Avenue regard-
ing his offer to clean up the pond in the South Paddock. He is a fine
young man and I consider his offer should be accepted. Mr. John Kearney
will give him every possible assistance.

summary: The Secretary/Manager had not yet arranged a meeting with Australian Bridge and Wharf management about the unsatisfactory Nielsen Park pile installation, so the bill remained unpaid.
red_flag_reason: A meeting with Australian Bridge and Wharf management had not yet been arranged and the bill remained unpaid.
quote:
I have not yet been able to arrange a meeting with the management
of Australian Bridge and Wharf regarding the unsatisfactory installation
of the new pile in the swimming area and the bill therefore remains unpaid.

summary: A very serious drain blockage around the Kiosk required the services of an electric eel.
quote:
A very serious drain blockage around the Kiosk necessitated the
services of an "electric eel".

summary: The usual summer outbreak of hooliganism required occasional intervention by the police.
red_flag_reason: Summer hooliganism required occasional police intervention.
quote:
The usual summer outbreak of "hooliganism" has required the occasional
intervention of the police.

summary: Water police raided Clark Island at night and made arrests; the Trust was patrolling on weekends and clearing garbage, stretching Nielsen staff to the limit.
red_flag_reason: Water police raided Clark Island and made arrests, while Nielsen staff were stretched to the limit by added patrols and garbage clearing.
quote:
Water police in the "Nemesis" raided the island during the hours of
darkness and made a number of arrests. Fortunately, there was no apparent
damage to Service installations on the island. We are now patrolling the
area on Saturdays and Sundays and clearing the garbage on Tuesday and
Wednesday of each week. The Nielsen staff is stretched to the limit.

summary: The Trust agreed to relieve Mr. Finlay from his Friends of Vaucluse House committee appointment and elected Mr. Herford to replace him.
quote:
(i) Mr. Finlay, due to pressure of professional work, asked
to be relieved from his position as one of the Trust's appointees
on the committee of the "Friends of Vaucluse House". The Trust
agreed to his request and Mr. Herford was unanimously elected
to replace him.

summary: Mr. Doyle outlined progress being made in organising the Friends function during the first quarter of 1975.
quote:
(ii) Mr. Doyle briefly outlined the progress being made in
organising the "Friends" function to be held during the first
quarter of 1975.

summary: The trustees agreed that Mr. Cook should pursue enquiries with the Australian National University to determine scientifically the date of manufacture of the Pompeian tiles.
quote:
(iii) It was agreed that Mr. Cook should pursue his en-
quiries with the Australian National University at Canberra
with a view to having the date of manufacture of the so called
"Pompeian" tiles scientifically determined. The Secretary/
Manager undertook to provide Mr. Cook with some broken pieces
of the tiles which he had stored in the office.

summary: Recoup summary 38 recorded expenditure from the Yerrinbee Historic Site advance account, including vouchers to David Cloonan Antiques, Wormald Bros., and J. & L.D. Andrew Pty. Ltd., with vouchers totalling $2,195.00 recouped on 7 December.
counterparty: David Cloonan Antiques; Wormald Bros.; J. & L.D. Andrew Pty. Ltd.

summary: The Trustees viewed a further letter from Mr. Harris, Solicitor, requesting extracts from Trust Minutes as an impertinence and left it to the President to reply as he thought fit.
red_flag_reason: A solicitor's request for extracts from Trust Minutes was viewed as an impertinence and left unresolved pending the President's reply.
quote:
1. A further letter from Mr. Harris, Solicitor asking for
extracts from Trust Minutes was viewed as an impertinence.
It was left to the President to reply as he thought fit.

summary: Proposal forms for revising Burglary and All Risks insurances were tabled, and the Secretary/Manager was to liaise with Mr. Doyle before completing and returning them to the G.I.O.
quote:
2. Proposal forms for revision of Burglary and "All Risks"
Insurances were tabled by the Secretary/Manager. It was
agreed that he should liaise with Mr. Doyle, and then com-
plete the forms and return them to the G.I.O.

summary: The Trust received a formal reply from the Town Clerk of Woollahra acknowledging the President's letter relating to the Tea Room.
quote:
3. A formal reply from the Town Clerk of Woollahra acknowledg-
ing receipt of the President's letter relating to the Tea
Room was received.

summary: A letter from Mr. John Cooper about the proposed licensed restaurant was read, and the Trustees agreed no reply was necessary because the party's official policy was neutral.
counterparty: Mr. John Cooper, Convenor of the Australia Party (Wentworth Group)
quote:
4. A copy of a letter from Mr. John Cooper, Convenor of the
Australia Party (Wentworth Group) to a Mrs. J. May of
Vaucluse regarding the proposed licensed restaurant was
read. It was agreed that no reply was necessary as the
purpose of the letter indicated that the official policy
of the Party in this matter was neutral.

summary: The Trust formally approved an ABC Television request for facilities to film the start of the Sydney-Hobart Yacht Race from Steele Point.
quote:
5. A letter from ABC - Television asking for the usual facilities
to film the start of the Sydney-Hobart Yacht Race from Steele
Point was received and formally approved.

asset: original portrait of Miss Edith Wentworth and painting The Three Fates
summary: The Trust approved payment of Mr. Setlik's account after he restored the original portrait of Miss Edith Wentworth and the painting The Three Fates, and expressed satisfaction that the paintings had been returned to the House.
quote:
6. A letter and invoice from Mr. Setlik, who had finished the
restoration of the original portrait of "Miss Edith Wentworth"
and the painting "The Three Fates" taken away some years
ago by a Mr. Byron, was received. The Secretary/Manager
advised that in his opinion Mr. Setlik's work was of the

summary: The Trust approved Mrs. M. Farrington's request for her daughter to be married in the grounds on 1 February 1975, while refusing a similar request from Mr. J. O'Keefe because it would cause too much disruption in the Park.
counterparty: Mrs. M. Farrington; Mr. J. O'Keefe
quote:
The Trust formally approved a request from a Mrs. M.
Farrington for her daughter to be quietly married in the
grounds on 1st February, 1975. A similar request from
Mr. J. O'Keefe - the rock and roll singer was refused on
the grounds that it would cause too much disruption in
the Park. It was left to the Secretary/Manager to write
suitable replies.

summary: The Treasurer reported that the Executive was satisfied with the caterers' operation of the Tea Room and had reached agreement in principle with Mr. N. Campbell on future glazing and restaurant toilets, but costs were not yet available and the Vice-President would meet Service Legal and the caterer's solicitor to clarify the lease points.
counterparty: Mr. N. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell Catering Company
red_flag_reason: Future glazing and toilet installation costs were not yet available, and the lease/licence terms needed further legal clarification.
quote:
On behalf of the Executive, the Treasurer then reported
on the meeting with Mr. N. Campbell - Manager of Michael
Avenell Catering Company. He said that the Executive
were more than satisfied with the manner in which the
caterers were operating the Tea Room and had reached agree-
ment in principle with Mr. Campbell relative to the future
glazing of the premises and the installation of the toilets
required for the proposed restaurant. Costs were not yet
available from the caterer's architect. Mr. Herford ex-
pressed the view that the caterers should be responsible for
insuring the new glazing when completed - it was agreed that
this should be noted for incorporation into the final lease.
The Treasurer further advised the meeting that Mr. Campbell
had accepted the Trust's recommendations and advice about
consulting Mr. K. Smithers when the time came to apply for
a win e licence for the new restaurant.

summary: The Secretary/Manager reported that no official notification had yet been received about vesting control of Nielsen Park in the Director, but Mr. Colin Green was understood to be appointed superintendent and would commence on 6 January 1975; the Trustees agreed no further action was possible then.
counterparty: Mr. Colin Green, new Superintendent of Sydney Harbour National Park
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that officially he had received
no notification to date from the Service regarding the pro-
posed vesting of the control of Nielsen Park in the Director,
but officially he understood that a Mr. Colin Green had
been appointed as the new Superintendent of Sydney Harbour
National Park and would commence his duties on the 6th
January, 1975. He anticipated that an official letter of
notification would be forthcoming from the Service in the
near future.

summary: The House Committee reported the purchase of a fine mid-19th century dresser for the kitchen and a small table, and the meeting unanimously approved the acquisitions.
quote:
(i) Mr. Herford reported the purchase of a very fine mid-
19th century dresser for the kitchen and a small table.
The meeting unanimously approved of these acquisitions and
the Secretary/Manager advised that he had already laid out
a selection of items from the Batterie de cuisine in the
glazed upper section of the dresser, which had in a short
space of time received much favourable comment from visitors.

asset: kitchen chimney breast and windshield wall
summary: Further development of the kitchen was hampered by the lack of an architect's decision on the chimney breast and windshield wall, so the Secretary/Manager was instructed to arrange for Mr. Lucas to attend the next Trust meeting and present a progress report.
red_flag_reason: Further development of the kitchen was hampered by the lack of an architect's decision on the chimney breast and windshield wall.
quote:
(ii) Mr. Herford also commented that further development
of the kitchen was hampered by lack of a decision by our
architect relative to the chimney breast and windshield
wall. The President said that this was one of the points
he would raise in an interview he intended having with Mr.
Lucas before the next meeting. Apart from arranging such
a meeting, the Secretary/Manager was instructed to ask Mr.
Lucas to attend the next Trust meeting and present a pro-
gress report on work done.

asset: Moreton Bay fig tree, Kiosk and patio
summary: The Grounds Committee noted concern that branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree could fall on the Kiosk and patio, and agreed to engage a tree surgeon to examine the tree and quote for lopping where necessary.
counterparty: Mr. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell Catering Company
red_flag_reason: Concern was raised that branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree could fall on the Kiosk and patio.
quote:
the danger of branches from the big Moreton Bay fig tree
falling on the Kiosk and the patio. It was agreed that we
should engage the services of a tree surgeon to examine
the tree and quote for "lopping" it where necessary.

summary: The Insurance, Legal and P.R. Committee reported that current legal matters had been dealt with in discussions relating to the Tea Room, and that Mr. Doyle was actively dealing with insurance matters and hoped to finalise adjustments with the G.I.O. soon.
quote:
Mr. Finlay advised that all current legal matters had been
dealt with in discussions relating to the Tea Room.

summary: The meeting endorsed the Secretary/Manager's interim contact with Artstaff over an inaccurate advertisement for the Longhurst Drawings portfolio and decided that a clause requiring Trust approval of proposed advertising copy should be added to the agreement.
red_flag_reason: An inaccurate Sydney Morning Herald advertisement by Artstaff could expose the Trust to criticism, so advertising copy needed prior Trust approval.
quote:
A badly worded and inaccurate advertisement in the "Sydney
Morning Herald" inserted by Artstaff Pty. Ltd., offering copies
of the portfolio for sale, had been noted by Trustees. The
Secretary/Manager advised that he had, as an interim measure,
contacted Artstaff and asked that any future proposed advert-
isements should be submitted to the Trust for approval prior
to publication. The meeting agreed that Artstaff were en-
titled to attempt to dispose of the 1,000 copies of the
portfolio, which they had retained, by any legitimate means
but the advertising copy must not leave the Trust open to
criticism. The meeting endorsed the action taken by the
Secretary/Manager, but considered it imperative that a clause
be added to the agreement making it mandatory for Artstaff
to submit any proposed advertising copy, relating to the
drawings, for Trust approval. The Secretary/Manager under-
took to contact the Service Legal Department and have a suit-
able clause added to the agreement.

summary: The Secretary/Manager was given permission to pay the Nielsen Park Pool storm-damage account, provided Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited gave a firm written undertaking to make the pile installation good at the end of the swimming season or before pool closure if necessary.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited
red_flag_reason: The pile installation was unsatisfactory and the storm-damage account was being settled only on the condition that the contractor make it good later if necessary.
quote:
In view of the desirability of settling this "storm damage"
account as soon as possible, the Secretary/Manager was
given permission to pay this account providing Australian
Bridge and Wharf Pty. Limited gave a firm written undertaking
to make it good at the end of the swimming season or at any
time prior to the closure of the pool should the necessity
arise. (Please see Secretary/Manager's current report).

summary: The financial report was accepted and recoup summaries 30 to 35 were formally confirmed by the meeting after having already been passed for payment by the N.P. & W.S.
quote:
The financial report was accepted and recoup summaries 30 to
35 were tabled. These had already been passed for payment
by the N.P. & W.S. and were formally confirmed by the meeting.

summary: The Trustees raised no objection to Avenell Catering inserting and paying for an advertisement for the House and Tea Room in the Sydney Morning Herald.
quote:
(i) Avenell Catering had asked if the Trust had any object-
ion to them inserting and paying for an advertisement for
the House and Tea Room in the columns of the Sydney Morning
Herald. No objection was raised and the Secretary/Manager
undertook to advise the catering company accordingly.

summary: The Trustees empowered the President to insert a suitable advertisement for the House in the Education Gazette when he thought fit.
quote:
(ii) The President considered that an advertisement for
the House in the "Education Gazette" might be useful. The
Trustees empowered the President to insert a suitable advert-
isement as and when he thought fit to do so.

summary: The meeting unanimously agreed that an invitation should be issued during 1975, at the President's discretion, to invite His Excellency the Governor of N.S.W., Sir Roden Cutler, to visit the House again.
counterparty: His Excellency, The Governor of N.S.W., Sir Roden Cutler
quote:
(iii) The President said that he felt it was time to invite
His Excellency, The Governor of N.S.W., Sir Roden Cutler
to visit the House again. The meeting agreed unanimously

summary: The Secretary/Manager's report noted leave arrangements for Mrs. Jean C'Connor, Mrs. O. Sames, Mrs. Phyllis Hall, and Mr. Tony Simpson over the Christmas and New Year period.
quote:
Mrs. Jean C'Connor proceeded on two weeks leave over the Christmas
and New Year period. Mrs. O. Sames took two weeks leave in mid January,1975.
Mrs. Phyllis Hall is currently on a fortnights leave and will return to duty
on the 10th February, 1975. Mr. Tony Simpson took a weeks leave over the
Christmas/New Year holiday period.

summary: A new heavy-duty electric power line had been laid to the House and a new pole and meter box installed, while tenders were called to re-asphalt the outer courtyard after the trench had settled for eight weeks.
quote:
(i) The new heavy duty electric power line has been laid to the House
and a new pole and meter box installed. Our line is no longer overloaded
and about 40% surplus power is now available for future use. The trench
cut across the outer courtyard has been allowed to settle for eight weeks
and tenders have now been called for re-asphalting the surface.

summary: An estimate had been called from Mr. Cameron for the installation, already approved by the Trustees, of security lighting around the verandah with the master switch in the Secretary/Manager's residence.
quote:
An estimate has also been called from Mr. Cameron for the installation
(already approved by the Trustees), of security lighting around the verandah
with the master switch in the Secretary/Manager's residence.

summary: Preparatory work for repainting the drawing room outer walls was underway, but large areas of drumming plaster required re-rendering to help overcome rising damp, and final paint selection awaited consultation with Berger's Paints.
counterparty: Mr. Lucas; Technical Department of Berger's Paints
red_flag_reason: Large areas of drumming plaster and rising damp were affecting the drawing room outer walls.
quote:
(ii) Preparatory work for the repainting of the outer walls of the
drawing room is under way, but we ran into trouble with LARGE areas of
"drumming"plaster. After taking advice from our architect, Mr. Lucas,
some large areas are being re-rendered with a mixture which will allow the
walls to "breathe" thus helping to overcome the problem of rising damp.
A final decision on the type of paint to be used will be made after consul-
tation with the Technical Department of Berger's Paints.

asset: covered walk-way, Stables and Boardroom external woodwork
summary: The covered walk-way in the courtyard had been repainted and other small painting jobs carried out, while quotations were called for repainting the external woodwork of the Stables and Boardroom.
quote:
(iii) The covered walk-way in the courtyard has been repainted and
other small painting jobs carried out. Quotations have been called for the
repainting of the external woodwork of the Stables and the Boardroom.

summary: Some velvet drapes around the staircase and windows had been taken down, dry cleaned and re-hung, with others to be progressively cleaned over the next few months.
quote:
(iv) Some of the velvet drapes around the staircase/windows have been
taken down, dry cleaned and re-hung. Others will be progressively cleaned
over the next few months.

asset: watercolours on loan to the House
summary: Representatives from the Art Gallery of N.S.W. examined the watercolours on loan to the House and were very happy with their condition.
quote:
(v) At my request representatives from the Art Gallery of N.S.W. have
examined the watercolours on loan to the House and are very happy with their
condition.

summary: Mr. Lucas and his assistant had spent considerable time at the House during January working on the architectural survey.
quote:
(vi) Mr. Lucas and his assistant have spent considerable time at the
House during January working on the architectural survey.

asset: skirting boards, architraves and Gilberthorpe's Room
summary: A supply of special mouldings had been obtained for renewing damaged skirting boards and architraves in the House and refurbishing Gilberthorpe's Room.
quote:
(vii) A supply of special mouldings have been obtained for the renewal
of damaged skirting boards and architraves in the House and the re-furbishing
of Gilberthorpe's Room.

summary: The opening into the loft from the old paint shop had been increased for easier storage access, while the staircase was being repaired and a handrail fitted.
quote:
(viii) The opening into the loft from the old paint shop has been
increased to permit easier access for storage purposes, the staircase is
being repaired and a handrail fitted.

summary: The Secretary/Manager discovered three more small areas of white ant activity, which were treated by Rentokil; the six-monthly inspection found no further activity but routine preventive measures were taken.
red_flag_reason: Three more small areas of white ant activity were discovered and had to be treated.
quote:
(ix) The writer discovered three more small areas of white ant activity
and these have been treated by Rentokil. Following this the six monthly
inspection taking three days was carried out. No further activity was dis-
covered, but routine preventive measures were taken.

summary: Despite prolonged dry weather, Mr. Kearney and his staff kept the gardens in good order with constant watering, but the south and west paddocks were in bad shape and two trees had crashed and been removed after high winds.
red_flag_reason: The south and west paddocks were in bad shape, and high winds had brought down broken branches and two crashed trees.
quote:
Despite the prolonged spell of dry weather Mr. Kearney and his staff
have kept the gardens in good order with constant watering, but the south
and west paddocks are in bad shape. High winds have on two occasions
littered the park with broken branches. Two trees have crashed and been
removed.

summary: On two consecutive Sundays early in January, complaints about nude sunbathers on the Beach Paddock were dealt with successfully without calling in the police.
quote:
On two consecutive Sundays early in January I received complaints about
nude sunbathers on the Beach Paddock and dealt successfully with the offenders
without having to call in the police.

asset: pond at the head of the South Paddock
summary: Volunteer worker Mr. Peter Jones had started cleaning up the pond at the head of the South Paddock and would continue the work in his spare time.
quote:
Our volunteer worker Mr. Peter Jones has made a start on cleaning up
the pond at the head of the South Paddock and will continue with this
work in his spare time.

summary: Because of difficulty disposing of large amounts of wet garbage from the Tea Room, Mr. Niel Campbell arranged for it to be removed three times weekly by disposal contractors.
quote:
For some time we had experienced great difficulty in disposing of the
large amounts of wet garbage from the Tea Room, consequently Mr. Niel Campbell
has arranged to have it removed thrice weekly by disposal contractors.

summary: Mr. Colin Green assumed control of Nielsen Park staff on 6 January 1975, but because he had no personal staff or facilities at Greycliffe House, the Secretary/Manager continued day-to-day administration; steps to legally invest Nielsen Park in the Director's care were likely to take at least another two months.
counterparty: Mr. Colin Green; Mr. George King
red_flag_reason: Legal investment of Nielsen Park in the Director's care was still pending, so the Trust remained legally responsible for Nielsen Park.
quote:
Officially the new Superintendent of Sydney Harbour National Park,
Mr. Colin Green assumed control over the staff of Nielsen Park on the
6th January, 1975, but at the same time Mr. George King - Assistant Director
had Mr. Green asked me to carry on with the day to day administration of
the two areas as Mr. Green at present has no personal staff or facilities
at Greycliffe House. This I agreed to do with the approval of the President.
I have established an excellent personal and working relationship with Mr.
Green and I know that our co-operation is greatly appreciated by the Service.

summary: December 1974 total income including admissions, sales and rents was $7,488.65, of which $6,216.81 was general revenue due to N.P. & W.S. and $1,271.84 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
Despite these setbacks total income inclusive of admissions, sales,
rents etc., was $7,488.65 of which General Revenue due to N.P. & W.S. was
$6,216.81 whilst $1,271.84 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.

summary: The Special Purposes Account was expected to have approximately $3,978.51 available at 1 January 1975, with anticipated cash flow of about $10,000.00 for the last six months of the financial year.
quote:
Therefore the approximate amount available in the Special Purposes Account
at 1.1.75 is $3,978.51. Anticipated cash flow into the account for the
last six months of the current financial year is approximately $10,000.00
hence the full amount available to cover expenditure until June, 1975 is
in the region of $14,000.00

summary: January 1975 total revenue including admissions, sales and rents was $14,961.24, of which $10,707.94 was general revenue due to N.P. & W.S. and $4,253.30 was credited to the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
Total revenue inclusive of admissions, sales, rents etc. was $14,961.24
of which general revenue due to N.P. & W.S. was $10,707.94 whilst $4,253.30
was credited to the Special Purposes Account.

summary: Because of unexpectedly high revenue, the cash available position was better than anticipated at the end of December 1974, with approximately $7,360.56 available in the Special Purposes Account at 1 February 1975.
quote:
Due to the somewhat unexpected high revenue the cash available
position is better than anticipated at the end of December, 1974. The
approximate amount available in the Special Purposes Account at 1.2.1975
is $7,360. 56
