summary: The amended tea-room lease had been held up in administration, but Bruce Wilson took it to the solicitors for Michael Avenell Catering Company and all parties were then understood to be satisfied with its terms.
quote:
<u>(a) Lease of Tea Room.</u>
In the absence of the Vice-Chairman who had been dealing directly
with the Legal Dept. of the Service in respect of the lease, Mr.
Doyle reported that there had been a hold-up of the amended lease
in the Administration Division, but Mr. Bruce Wilson of the Legal
Department had personally taken it to the solicitors for Michael
Avenell Catering Company and it was understood that all parties
were now satisfied with the terms of the amended lease.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room
summary: The Trust accepted Adan Tree Service's $550.00 quotation to trim the Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room and ordered the work to be carried out as soon as possible.
quote:
<u>(b) Trimming or Loretto La. Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room.</u>
It was agreed that the quotation from Adan Tree Service for trimm-
ing this tree, in the sum of $550.00 should be accepted and an order
placed for the work to be carried out as soon as possible.

summary: The jury-rig supporting the Nielsen Park Pool nets was holding, and an arrangement had been made with Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. to drive a new pile later in the season or sooner if the rig failed; payment for the unsatisfactory pile was withheld.
counterparty: Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. Pty. Ltd.
red_flag_reason: The pool pile was unsatisfactory and the supporting jury-rig was still needed, so payment for the pile was withheld while a new pile awaited installation.
quote:
<u>(c) Nielsen Park Pool - Collapsed Pile</u>
The Secretary/Manager amplified the remarks in his report for
December '74/January '75 and advised that the jury-rig erected by
the staff to support the nets was holding well and that he had
come to an arrangement with Australian Bridge and Wharf Co. Pty.
Ltd., to have a new pile driven either at the end of the swimming
season or sooner if the jury-rig collapsed at an earlier date.
Payment for the installation of the unsatisfactory pile has been
withheld.

summary: Woollahra Council rescinded its opposition to the proposed restaurant wine licence and would remain neutral, and the Trust confirmed that the Catering Company should seek licence operating hours from 12.00 noon to 3.00 p.m.
quote:
(i) A letter from the Town Clerk of Woollahra Council was read indicat-
ing that they would not support the "Vaucluse House Protection
Campaign" in their objection to a proposed wine licence for the
restaurant, but would act independently when the application came
before the Licencing Court. (Subsequently, at a further meeting
of Council the motion to oppose the licence was rescinded meaning
that the Council would remain neutral.) All Trustees present
expressed satisfaction at Council's decision.
The prime mover in bringing about the recision motion was Alderman
Johnson. It was felt that the Trust could not thank the Alderman
in writing and therefore Mr. Doyle was empowered to thank him
verbally on behalf of the Trust.
It was confirmed that the Catering Company, when applying for a
liquor licence, should ask for the operating hours to be from 12.00
noon to 3.00 p.m. However in the light of new legislation in
State Parliament it was likely that the court would grant longer
hours if they agreed to the application for a licence, but this
would still leave the Trust with the power to restrict trading
hours by agreement with the Catering Company.

summary: The Trust agreed to acknowledge the Vaucluse House Protection Campaign's survey and plan politely while continuing to support the caterers' application for a liquor licence.
quote:
(ii) A letter from the Secretary of the "Vaucluse House Protection
Campaign" enclosing the results of a survey of residents, relative
to the proposed application for a liquor licence for the restaurant,
was tabled, together with a further document entitled "A Plan for
Vaucluse".
It was agreed that receipt of the above should be politely acknow-
ledged but indicating that the Trust would continue to support
the caterers in any application for a liquor licence.

summary: Because Dinkel's letter made no specific recommendations, Mr. Herford was to call on him in England to seek recommendations about restoring the kitchen area.
quote:
(iii) A letter from Mr. J.A.H. Dinkel, Keeper of the Royal Pavilion,
Brighton, England, replying to enquiries made by the Secretary/
Manager regarding the restoration of the kitchen area, was read.
The reply made no specific recommendations, but it was understood
that Mr. Herford who was on his way to England, would call upon
Mr. Dinkel to see if, in a personal interview, he could perhaps
put forward some recommendations.

summary: The meeting read and accepted the Service Director's letter appointing Colin Green as District Superintendent of Sydney Harbour National Park.
quote:
(iv) A letter from the Director of the Service relating to the appoint-
ment of Mr. Colin Green as District Superintendent, Sydney Harbour
National Park was read and accepted.

summary: The minimum order of three gross for Wentworth Coat-of-Arms souvenir glassware was considered too large, so the Secretary/Manager was empowered to negotiate a smaller mixed-line order.
quote:
(v) The Secretary/Manager tabled a letter and catalogue he had received
from Permanent Print (Ceramics) Pty. Limited regarding souvenir
glassware bearing the Wentworth Coat-of-Arms. It was felt that a
minimum order of 3 gross of any one line was too great for our
limited sales facilities, but the Secretary/Manager was empowered
to negotiate if possible for a smaller minimum number of mixed
lines.

summary: The Trust accepted R.T. Houghton's quotation of $1,200.00 to repaint the external woodwork of the stables.
quote:
(vi) Quotations from R.T. Houghton for the re-painting of the external
woodwork of the stables and the boardroom in the sums of $1,200.00
and $332.00 were accepted.

summary: The Trust accepted R.T. Houghton's $332.00 quotation to repaint the external woodwork of the boardroom.
quote:
(vi) Quotations from R.T. Houghton for the re-painting of the external
woodwork of the stables and the boardroom in the sums of $1,200.00
and $332.00 were accepted.

asset: two-seater Victorian Toilet and old bricks
summary: The Trust agreed that the two-seater Victorian Toilet and old bricks should be put into safe storage until a more secure display position could be allocated.
red_flag_reason: The display items in the saddle-room were not securely displayed, so they needed safe storage pending a more secure display position.
quote:
(vii) A letter from the Secretary of the "Friends of Vaucluse House"
was read regarding the security of the two-seater Victorian Toilet
and old bricks presently displayed in the saddle-room of the
stables and also referring to the fact, already known to the Trustees,
that the guttering on the stables was not of 19th century design.
The Secretary/Manager then read notes he had made relating to the
points raised in the letter and as he would be proceeding on leave
the following day the President kindly offered to frame a suitable
reply.
It was further agreed that the toilets and bricks should be put
into safe storage pending the allocation of a more secure display
position.

summary: There was nothing further to discuss about Sydney Harbour National Park because the Director's letter had already been read under correspondence.
quote:
<u>(a) Sydney Harbour National Park.</u>
There was nothing further to discuss as the Director's letter had
been read under "Correspondence".

summary: The Trust approved Wormald Bros.' quotation of $354.00 per annum for a comprehensive maintenance contract for the new fire alarm system.
quote:
<u>(b) Fire Alarm System</u>
The quotation from Wormald Bros. for a comprehensive maintenance
contract for the new Fire Alarm System in the sum of $354.00 per
annum was approved.

summary: The Friends of Vaucluse House barbecue was proceeding according to plan, and the Secretary/Manager had left written instructions for security, car parking and staffing because he would be on leave on 1 March 1975.
quote:
<u>(c) Friends of Vaucluse House, Barbecue(1.3.75)</u>
Mr. Doyle advised that the organisation of this event was pro-
ceeding according to plan and he anticipated a very successful
evening providing the weather was fine. The Secretary/Manager
advised that as he would be on leave on 1.3.75, he had left full
written instructions regarding security arrangements, car parking
etc. with his assistant - Mrs. P. Hall and had made arrangements
for all necessary staff to be on duty.

summary: The Trustees were satisfied with Clive Lucas's interim architectural survey report and agreed to submit copies of the final Stage 1 report to Mr. Webber and Mr. Fisher.
quote:
The Trustees were well satisfied with the most excellent presentation
of his interim report, by Mr. Clive Lucas, and looked forward to
finalisation of this first stage of the survey, with measured drawings,
in the near future. It was agreed that copies of the final report
on Stage 1 should be submitted to our Honorary Consultant Arch-
itect - Mr. Webber and to the Consultant Architect of the N.P. & W.S.
Mr. Fisher.

summary: Mrs. Couzens was not prepared to sell her Davenport desk to the Trust because she might bequeath it to her grandson, so the matter was left in abeyance.
quote:
As Mr. Cook had been on holiday and Mr. Herford was now on leave
the only matter to report was that Mrs. Couzens was not at the
moment prepared to sell her "Davenport" desk to the Trust as she
might bequeath it to her grandson. It was decided to leave this
matter in abeyance.

summary: The Trust agreed to plant gum trees and other native flora around the South Paddock perimeter to replace dead trees when money became available for reconstituting that section of the Park.
red_flag_reason: Replacement planting of the South Paddock perimeter was postponed until money became available.
quote:
Mr. Barrett mentioned that consideration should be given to the
planting of gum trees and other native flora around the periphery
of the South Paddock to replace trees which had died over the
years. It was agreed that this should be done when money became
available for the reconstitution of this section of the Park.

summary: Mr. Doyle expected to finalise increased insurance premiums with the G.I.O., noting that the new fire alarm system would give substantial rebates and favourable terms had been negotiated for the House, contents and ancillary buildings.
quote:
Legal matters in connection with the lease of the tea room had
already been dealt with under correspondence. Mr. Doyle advised that
he was now almost ready to finalise the increased insurance premiums
with the G.I.O. as the Inspector had been out to the House on the
14th January. The installation of the new fire alarm system would
give us substantial rebates on the Fire Policy and he had negotiated
very favourable terms on the insurance of the House and its contents
and on ancilliary buildings.

summary: Mr. Cook reported that small advertisements in This Week in Sydney had been arranged and that the brochure included a sizeable editorial mention.
quote:
Mr. Cook who had arranged a series of small advertisements in "This
Week in Sydney" produced copies of the brochure in which we had
also been given a sizeable mention in the editorial.

summary: The Secretary/Manager's report was accepted, but Mr. Crouch suggested that estimates for resurfacing the driveway and outer courtyard should also be sought from Allen Bros. and Bitupave.
quote:
This, having been circulated, was accepted by the meeting, but
with regard to the calling of quotations for the re-surfacing
of the driveway and outer courtyard adjacent to the Olola Avenue
entrance Mr. Crouch suggested that estimates should also be sought
from Allen Bros. and Bitupave.

summary: It was agreed to install a time clock in the verandah security lighting circuit for the small extra cost involved.
quote:
Insofar as the security lighting around the verandah of the House
was concerned, it was suggested that for the small extra cost involved
the installation of a time clock in the circuit would be useful.
It was agreed that this be done.

summary: The financial reports for December 1974 and January 1975 were accepted, and recoupment summaries 36 to 53, already passed for payment by N.P. & W.S., were formally confirmed.
quote:
The financial reports for December, 1974 and January 1975 were
accepted and recoupment summaries 36 to 53, which had already been
passed for payment by the N.P. & W.S., were formally confirmed by
the meeting.

summary: The President had congratulated Mr. Lewis and Mr. Morris on their appointments and invited Mr. Morris to meet the Trust at a later date.
quote:
The President advised the meeting that, on behalf of the Trust,
he had congratulated Mr. Lewis on his appointment to the Premier-
ship of N.S.W. and also Mr. Morris on his appointment as the new
Minister of Lands. Both letters had received suitable acknowledg-
ment. The President also indicated that he had invited Mr. Morris
to meet the Trust at a later date.

summary: The Friends of Vaucluse House formally expressed full support for the Trust regarding the proposed restaurant liquor licence application.
quote:
Mr. Doyle advised the meeting that as a body, the "Friends of
Vaucluse House" had formally expressed their full support of
the Trust regarding the proposed application for a liquor licence
for the restaurant.

summary: Mr. Snelling reported progress preparing the two exhibition rooms adjacent to the Blue Mountains Exhibition room.
quote:
Mr. Snelling reported on the progress made in preparing the two
exhibition rooms adjacent to the Blue Mountains Exhibition room.

summary: The meeting agreed to relieve the President from regular attendance at Friends of Vaucluse House Committee meetings, while he would remain an ex-officio member.
quote:
The meeting considered that there was no alternative but to agree
with the President's request although he would still remain an
ex-officio member of the "Friends" Committee, in the same way as
he was an ex-officio member of all Trust sub-committees.

summary: The Trust drew attention to the dangerous stump of the original Nielsen Park Pool concrete pile and agreed to have the appropriate service officer examine it; Sydney Bridge and Wharf could remove or make it safe when reinstalling the collapsed pile.
red_flag_reason: The original concrete pile stump was in a dangerous state and needed removal or making safe when the collapsed pile was reinstalled.
quote:
<u>(a) Nielsen Park Pool - collapsed pile</u>
The President drew the attention of the Trust to the danger-
ous state of the stump of the original concrete pile. It
was agreed that the appropriate service officer's attention
should be drawn to this matter. The Secretary/Manager
advised that Sydney Bridge and Wharf had indicated that
they could remove this or render it safe when they re-in-
stalled the collapsed pile.

summary: Mr. Doyle reported that he had personally thanked Alderman Johnson for helping effect the rescission of Woollahra Council's motion about the proposed restaurant wine licence.
quote:
<u>(b) Woollahra Council - rescission of motion re proposed wine licence
for restaurant</u>
Mr. Doyle advised the meeting that, as requested by the
Trust, he had personally thanked Alderman Johnson for the
part he had played in effecting this rescission.

summary: The Friends of Vaucluse House barbecue was highly successful, with about 250 adults and 150 children attending, total income around $3,000.00, and about half expected as clear profit; the President was to thank the committee.
quote:
<u>(c) Friends of Vaucluse House Barbecue</u>
Mr. Doyle, in his capacity of Chairman of the "Friends",
reported that the event had been highly successful with an
attendance of approximately 250 adults and 150 children.
Total income was in the region of $3,000.00 of which
approximately 50% should be clear profit.
It was agreed that the President should write a letter of
appreciation of the effort put in by the Committee of the
"Friends".

summary: The Secretary/Manager was to contact the Minister of Lands' secretary to arrange a visit, and the Minister subsequently indicated he wished to visit on Monday 7 April at 3 p.m.
quote:
<u>(d) Invitation to the new Minister of Lands to visit the House.</u>
It was resolved that the Secretary/Manager should contact
the Minister's secretary with a view to arranging a visit
on either the 10th, 23rd April or the 1st May. (Subsequently
the Minister indicated that he wished to visit the House
on Monday, 7th April at 3 p.m. All members of the Board
have agreed with this time and date by telephone and the
Trust will take afternoon tea with the Minister.)

summary: The President read his reply to Mrs. Simpson's letter, and the Trustees approved the reply.
quote:
(1) The President read his reply to Mrs. Simpson's letter
tabled at the previous meeting. The Trustees expressed
their approval of this reply.

summary: The President read two letters from Mrs. May of the Vaucluse House Protection Campaign about the proposed restaurant licence and other park matters, and his reply received the meeting's full approval.
quote:
(2) The President read two letters from Mrs. May, Hon. Sec-
retary of the so called "Vaucluse House Protection Campaign"
re the proposed restaurant licence and other matters
relating to Vaucluse and Nielsen Parks in general. He then
read his reply which received the full approval of the
meeting.

summary: Permission was granted for Pendragon Films to use the House and grounds as a film location at the usual minimum fee of $100 for the first four hours, plus $25 per additional hour or part hour.
quote:
(3) A letter was tabled from Pendragon Films Pty. Limited,
seeking permission to use the House and grounds as a
location for a film sequence. Permission was granted
at the usual fee of $100. minimum, covering the first
four hours of filming plus $25 per hour or part of an
hour for any additional time.

asset: roofs over the west wing and gardener's cottage
summary: The Trust accepted two quotations from A.J.E. Henry and Son and Master Slaters for immediate roof repairs over the west wing and gardener's cottage in the total sum of $105.
counterparty: A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters
quote:
(4) Four quotations from A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters,
for various repair work to roofs were considered. It was
resolved to accept two, immediately covering repairs to
the roofs over the west wing and the gardener's cottage
in the total sum of $105. It was decided to defer the
making of a decision on the repairs to the kitchen roof,
as an examination had shown that all nails had rusted
away, flashings required renewal and some battens needed
replacement. This involved a quoted expenditure of
$3256.62 which could not be met out of currently available
funds. It was agreed that this quotation should form the
basis for the request of special funds from the Service
in the 1975/6 budget.

summary: The Trust deferred a decision on kitchen roof repairs because the $3,256.62 quotation could not be met from current funds, and agreed to use the quotation as the basis for requesting special funds in the 1975/6 budget.
counterparty: A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters
red_flag_reason: The kitchen roof needed rusted nails replaced, flashings renewed and battens replaced, and the $3,256.62 quoted cost could not be met from currently available funds.
quote:
(4) Four quotations from A.J.E. Henry and Son, Master Slaters,
for various repair work to roofs were considered. It was
resolved to accept two, immediately covering repairs to
the roofs over the west wing and the gardener's cottage
in the total sum of $105. It was decided to defer the

as an examination had shown that all nails had rusted

replacement. This involved a quoted expenditure of
$3256.62 which could not be met out of currently available

basis for the request of special funds from the Service
in the 1975/6 budget.

asset: tractor link rake and grader blade
summary: The Trust accepted Deveson Jahn's $1,030 quotation for a link rake and grader blade for use with the tractor in beach cleaning and other park work.
quote:
(5) A quotation from Deveson Jahn (Aust) Pty. Ltd. for a
link rake and grader blade for use with the tractor in
beach cleaning and other work around the park, in the
sum of $1030, was considered and accepted.

summary: The meeting agreed that Clive Lucas was performing the architectural survey satisfactorily and raised the ceiling cost for completing Stage 1 from $2,500 to $3,000.
quote:
The President surveyed the progress made to date and
read the latest letter from Mr. Lucas. After some dis-
cussion the meeting agreed that Mr. Lucas was performing
the survey in a most diligent and satisfactory manner.
It was further agreed that the "ceiling" cost for the
completion of Stage 1 of the survey should be raised
from $2,500 to $3,000.

summary: The five-year plan, previously put in abeyance because of the economic climate, was to be restarted for 1975-80, and the Secretary/Manager was authorised to advise the Director that previous submissions needed little amendment.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager advised that this plan, which had
been put in abeyance because of the economic climate
appertaining in the latter half of 1974 was to be re-
started and would now cover the years 1975-80. It was
agreed that our previous submissions needed little amend-
ment and the Secretary/Manager was authorised to advise
the Director accordingly.

summary: The Trust approved payment of $556.20, representing long-service leave due to the widow or nearest legal representative of former Nielsen Park foreman Mr. Irvine, to Mrs. A. York.
quote:
(c) The Secretary/Manager advised that he had received a
letter from the Service indicating that a sum of $556.20,
representing a balance of long service leave, was due to
the widow or nearest legal representative of Mr. Irvine
(deceased) a former foreman at Nielsen Park. Mrs. Irvine
had been traced by the Secretary/Manager; she had re-
married and was now known as Mrs. A. York, and he sought
the formal approval of the Trust to pay the sum due, to
her. Approval was given.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room
summary: The Moreton Bay Fig Tree had been examined by Duncan Campbell, who was obtaining a second opinion from M. Watson; the meeting agreed to act on Campbell's advice when received.
quote:
The President advised that, since the last meeting, the
tree had been examined by Mr. Duncan Campbell - the tree
expert of the N.P. & W.S., who was obtaining a second
opinion from Mr. M. Watson of the Royal Botanic Gardens.
Mr. Campbell's official report was expected during the
week following the meeting: it was unanimously agreed
that his advice, when received, should be acted upon.

summary: The House Committee recommended that all Trustees look for furniture suitable for the kitchen area, and the meeting agreed to do so.
quote:
The committee felt that all Trustees should now keep
their eyes open for furniture suitable for the kitchen
area. It was agreed that this should be done.

asset: kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and hot water cistern
summary: Mr. Herford stressed the need for definite decisions from Clive Lucas about the kitchen fireplace, chimney breast and hot water cistern before re-furnishing plans could be made, and the Secretary/Manager was instructed to pursue the matter.
quote:
Mr. Herford once again stressed the urgency of obtaining
some definite decisions from Mr. Lucas regarding the fire-
place, chimney breast and hot water cistern in the kitchen
as no plans for re-furnishing could be made until such
decisions had been made. The Trust agreed with Mr. Herford
and the Secretary/Manager was instructed to pursue this
matter with the architect.

asset: outer courtyard at Olola Avenue entrance
summary: Although A.R.C. Asphalting and Bitupave had taken details of the outer courtyard work, quotations had not yet been received and no action could be taken until they were available.
quote:
Although two firms, A.R.C. Asphalting and Bitupave had
taken details of the work required in the outer courtyard
(Olola Avenue entrance) quotations had yet to be received.
No action could be taken until these were to hand.

summary: The meeting agreed that, when the Park perimeter was cleared, a variety of Australian gums should be used for re-afforestation of the area.
quote:
The trimming of the Moreton Bay Fig Tree had already been
dealt with under general business. The meeting agreed that,
when the periphery of the Park was cleared, a variety of
Australian gums should be used for re-afforestation of
the area.

summary: Mr. Doyle reported that everything was now in order with the Trust's insurances.
quote:
Mr. Doyle reported that everything was now in order with
our insurances.

summary: The meeting endorsed a further series of advertisements in This Week in Sydney and instructed the Secretary/Manager to make the necessary arrangements.
quote:
It was recommended that a further series of advertisements
should be inserted in "This week in Sydney". The meeting
endorsed this recommendation and the Secretary/Manager
instructed to make the necessary arrangements.

summary: The meeting agreed to forward to the Service a recommendation for a combined Service advertisement in the Sydney Morning Herald at holiday times.
quote:
Mr. Barrett made the suggestion that a combined Service's
advertisement at holiday times in the appropriate columns
of the Sydney Morning Herald could have merit. The meeting
agreed that a recommendation for this form of advertising
should be forwarded to the Service.

summary: Recoupment summaries Nos. 54 to 60 were tabled and formally approved by the meeting.
quote:
Recoup summaries Nos. 54 to 60 were tabled and formally
approved by the meeting.

summary: The Treasurer reported that, with prudent management, the Special Purposes Account had adequate funds for projects planned for the remainder of the current financial year.
quote:
The Treasurer gave a brief summary of the position relating
to the Special Purposes Account which showed that, with
prudent management, we had adequate funds in this account
to carry out projects planned for the remainder of the
current financial year.

summary: The meeting endorsed seeking the aid of a Mitchell Library staff member for historical research at an appropriate fee, and the President would approach Mr. Doust about it.
quote:
The President suggested that it could be advantageous to
attempt to enlist the aid of a member of the staff of the
Mitchell Library for historical research, from time to
time, at an appropriate fee. The meeting endorsed this
recommendation and the President undertook to approach
Mr. Doust to ascertain if this was possible.

summary: The Chairman asked members to consider charging a car parking fee in Vaucluse Park so the matter could be discussed at the next Trust meeting.
quote:
The Chairman then asked members to give consideration to
the charging of a car parking fee in Vaucluse Park so
that the matter could be discussed at the next Trust
meeting.

summary: Mr. Snelling reported progress preparing the new exhibition rooms, and Mr. Cook said the rooms would be of great interest to visitors when opened.
quote:
Mr. Snelling reported the progress being made with the
preparation of the new exhibition rooms and Mr. Cook
who had visited the rooms to advise Mr. Snelling on one
or two points expressed the view that these rooms would
be of great interest to visitors when opened.

summary: The Trust recommended employing professional removalists to move the sideboard from the Guests' Dining-room to Greycliffe House and the replacement sideboard from the Museum Rooms to the Guests' Dining-room.
quote:
The Trust also recommended that professional removalists
be employed to move the sideboard from the Guests' Dining-
room to Greycliffe House and the sideboard to replace it
from the Museum Rooms to the Guests' Diningroom.

summary: The major restoration work on the north front of the House had been completed, and external wall work in the office area was expected to be completed during April unless unforeseen problems arose.
quote:
(i) The major part of the restoration work on the north front of
the House has been completed and it is anticipated that unless unforeseen
problems come to light, the work on the external walls of the office area
will be completed during April. Berger's Technical Department has been
consulted and have advised that acrylic paint will be suitable for the
re-painting of these walls and will allow the newly rendered areas to
"breathe" and will also adhere to the old gloss painted areas. Mr. Lucas
has suggested a light stone colour for your consideration.

summary: Service-appointed photographers had re-photographed the interior and exterior of the House and other buildings for a new colour folder and postcards, with all costs to be borne by the Service.
quote:
(ii) During the month Service appointed photographers have re-photo-
graphed the interior and exterior of the House and other buildings in
preparation for the printing of an entirely new colour folder and post-
cards for sale at the desk. It is hoped that proofs will be available
in time for the next board meeting. All costs will be borne by the
Service.

summary: Preparatory work for repainting the stables was under way, and colours suggested by Mr. Lucas would be available for consideration at the Board meeting.
quote:
(iii) Preparatory work for the re-painting of the stables is under
way and colours suggested by Mr. Lucas will be available for your con-
sideration at the Board meeting.

summary: After the heavy bay-window restoration work, contract carpenter Ivor Wilson began replacing termite-damaged panelling and architraves using special mouldings copied by Tanner & Middleton and Western Red Cedar timber.
quote:
(iv) With the completion of the heavy work on the restoration of
the bay windows in the Drawing Room, our contract carpenter, Mr. Ivor
Wilson has been able to turn his attention to other work and a start has
been made on the replacement of termite damaged panelling and architraves
in the House, using the special new mouldings faithfully copied from the
original by Tanner & Middleton. All timber restoration work is being
carried out in Western Red Cedar as approved by Mr. Lucas.

summary: The two-seater toilet formerly housed in the stables had been put into safe storage.
quote:
(v) The two seater toilet formerly housed in the stables has been
put into safe storage.

summary: The carillon clock was once more in position on the Family Dining Room mantelpiece, fully operational and attracting visitors.
quote:
(vi) The carillon clock is once more in position on the mantlepiece
of the Family Dining Room. It is fully operational and proving a great
attraction to visitors.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room
summary: Duncan Campbell's report on the Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room was to hand and would be tabled under correspondence at the next meeting.
quote:
(i) Mr. Duncan Campbell's report on the Moreton Bay Fig Tree ad-
jacent to the Tea Room is to hand and will be tabled under correspondence
at the next meeting.

summary: With autumn clearing work in the grounds commenced, the new tractor link-rake had proved useful for beach cleaning and gathering twigs and leaves, particularly on the South Paddock.
quote:
(ii) With the advent of autumn, clearing work in the grounds has
commenced. The new link-rake for the tractor has already proved its
worth not only for beach cleaning but for the rapid gathering up of twigs
and leaves particularly on the South Paddock.

asset: Nielsen Park Dressing sheds and Pool
summary: Nielsen Park Dressing sheds and Pool were scheduled to close down at 6.0 p.m. on Sunday 13 April 1975 in accordance with established practice.
quote:
In accordance with established practice Nielsen Park Dressing
sheds and Pool will close down at 6.0 p.m. on Sunday, the 13th
April, 1975.

asset: Clark Island wharf and water storage tank
summary: Clark Island had been closed to the public while a new wharf was built and a larger water storage tank installed, and the Trust was no longer concerned with its supervision.
quote:
Clark Island has been closed to the public whilst a new wharf
is built and a larger water storage tank installed. We are now no
longer concerned with its supervision.

summary: The executive decided that the Secretary/Manager should handle the general administration budget section, adjusting for inflation and noting that Nielsen Park running expenses would not be borne by the Trust next year.
quote:
After a general discussion on the items coming under this heading it
was decided that as this section of the budget primarily concerned re-
curring expenses, the Secretary/Manager should deal with it making the
necessary adjustments to take account of inflationary trends and also
bearing in mind that the expenses of running Nielsen Park will not be
borne by the Trust in the next financial year.

summary: The executive decided to ask for at least $8,000.00 to cover stores, stationery, office furniture and minor plant in the 1975-76 budget.
quote:
However, it was decided that we should ask for $8,000.00 minimum
to cover stores, stationery, office furniture, minor plant etc. (Schedule
No. 21) and $2,000.00 for advertising (Schedule No. 24). The allowances
in 1974/75 for these two items were respectively $4,000.00 and $250.00
which had put an unwarranted drain on the Special Purposes Account dur-
ing the current financial year.

summary: The executive decided to ask for $2,000.00 for advertising in the 1975-76 budget.
quote:
However, it was decided that we should ask for $8,000.00 minimum
to cover stores, stationery, office furniture, minor plant etc. (Schedule
No. 21) and $2,000.00 for advertising (Schedule No. 24). The allowances
in 1974/75 for these two items were respectively $4,000.00 and $250.00
which had put an unwarranted drain on the Special Purposes Account dur-
ing the current financial year.

summary: The executive decided to ask for $9,000.00 for building maintenance in the 1975-76 budget, compared with the 1973-74 allocation of $5,000.00.
quote:
During the present financial year, at the request of the Director,
the first two became fully chargeable to the Special Purposes Account
and in view of the current very substantial nature of this account
(approximately $24,000 p.a.)it is anticipated that much general mainten-
ance of buildings and park facilities will remain chargeable to this
account, especially in view of the fact that major restoration and
development work comes under the five year plan and will be the sub-
ject of special grants (Schedule Item 29). Nevertheless we would have
nothing to lose by asking for funds to cover these two items and it
was decided to ask for $9,000.00 for Building Maintenance (Schedule Item
10) (1973-74 allocation was $5,000.00) and $7,000.00 for park maintenance
(Schedule Item 28) (1973-74 allocation was also $7,000.00, but this in-
cluded Nielsen Park).

summary: The executive decided to ask for $7,000.00 for park maintenance in the 1975-76 budget, the same as the 1973-74 allocation that had included Nielsen Park.
quote:
During the present financial year, at the request of the Director,
the first two became fully chargeable to the Special Purposes Account
and in view of the current very substantial nature of this account
(approximately $24,000 p.a.)it is anticipated that much general mainten-
ance of buildings and park facilities will remain chargeable to this
account, especially in view of the fact that major restoration and
development work comes under the five year plan and will be the sub-
ject of special grants (Schedule Item 29). Nevertheless we would have
nothing to lose by asking for funds to cover these two items and it
was decided to ask for $9,000.00 for Building Maintenance (Schedule Item
10) (1973-74 allocation was $5,000.00) and $7,000.00 for park maintenance
(Schedule Item 28) (1973-74 allocation was also $7,000.00, but this in-
cluded Nielsen Park).

summary: The executive decided to apply for funds to purchase a 30 cwt truck because the Trust could not always rely on borrowing one from Sydney Harbour National Park after Nielsen Park was hived off.
quote:
It was decided to apply for funds to purchase a 30 cwt truck
(schedule Item 27), as with the pending "hiveing off" of Nielsen Park
we cannot always rely on being able to borrow one from Sydney Harbour
National Park even though we currently have a most excellent working
arrangement with the District Superintendent.

summary: The executive would re-apply for replacement of the 14-year-old tractor, which was approaching the end of its economic life.
red_flag_reason: The tractor was 14 years old and approaching the end of its economic life, so replacement funding was being sought.
quote:
We will also re-apply for the replacement of the tractor
which is 14 years old and hence approaching the end of its economic
life.

summary: The meeting welcomed the Minister for Lands' letter expressing satisfaction with his 7 April 1975 visit and the Trustees' preservation efforts.
quote:
1. The President read a letter from the Minister for Lands
expressing great satisfaction with his visit on the 7th
April, 1975. The meeting warmly welcomed the Minister's
appreciation of the efforts being made by the Trustees in
the preservation of the House.

summary: The Secretary/Manager reported that the $556.20 long service leave payment due to the next of kin of the late Mr. Frank Irvine had been paid to his widow.
quote:
2. The Secretary/Manager advised that the $556.20 long service
leave payment due to the next of kin of the late Mr. Frank
Irvine of Nielsen Park staff had been paid to his widow.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room
summary: Mr. Ralph Clark's recommendations to trim the Moreton Bay Fig Tree were accepted, and the later report records that the $1,500 order for the work had been placed.
red_flag_reason: The tree was described as a considerable hazard and its complete safety could not be guaranteed.
quote:
<u>3. Trimming of Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to Tea Room.</u>
Mr. Ralph Clark - the tree surgeon recommended by the Service
was in attendance and with the aid of photographs explained
what he considered was necessary to improve the health of this
tree and to make it considerably less of a hazard than it is
at the present time. He stressed that it was impossible for
anyone to guarantee complete safety of such a large and old
tree, but the treatment he was suggesting would, he considered,
extend the healthy life of the tree by approximately 100 years.
After some close questioning by the Vice-President and Mr.
Herford, it was agreed that Mr. Clark's recommendations should
be accepted and that the Executive should act upon his written
report and quotation for carrying out the work as soon as it
was received.

summary: The meeting noted that Mr. Doust agreed to casual employment of his staff for historical research and left the President to contact Miss Yvonne Brown.
quote:
<u>1. Historical Research</u>
Two letters from Mr. Doust - Principal Librarian of New
South Wales, responding to one written by the President
regarding the casual employment of one of Mr. Doust's staff
to carry out historical research from time to time, were read.
It was noted with satisfaction that Mr. Doust agreed to the
request and it was left to the President to contact the nominee,
a Miss Yvonne Brown.

summary: The meeting agreed to all Director requests concerning full transfer of Nielsen Park management to the District Superintendent on 1 May 1975.
quote:
<u>2. Sydney Harbour National Park.</u>
A letter from the Director regarding the assumption of full
control of the management of Nielsen Park on the 1st May,
1975 by the District Superintendent was received and agree-
ment given to all requests made by the Director. The Secret-
ary/Manager was instructed to make a suitable reply.

summary: The Trust gave qualified approval to APA Leisure Time International Limited's request to make a commercial television film, with no filming in the House.
quote:
The Trust gave qualified approval to a request from APA
Leisure Time International Limited to make a commercial
television film for release in Hong Kong advertising Marlboro
cigarettes, but no filming was to take place in the House.

summary: The meeting deferred the Tea Room lease matter to the Legal Committee and Secretary/Manager, with an extraordinary meeting possible if contentious lease problems arose.
red_flag_reason: The Tea Room lease was unresolved because the Director's draft lease and the caterer's future proposals required legal action, and contentious lease problems could require an extraordinary meeting.
quote:
Two letters were tabled, one from the Director enclosing a
draft copy of the proposed lease and the other from Mr.
Campbell of Michael, Avenell Catering with supporting docu-
ments and plans showing what had been done in the Tea Room
since they took over its operation on the 18th October, 1975,
and proposals for the future with particular reference to
the establishment of a restaurant in addition to the Tea Room.

summary: The meeting endorsed the Executive's 1975-6 budget recommendations and directed the Secretary/Manager to prepare detailed documents for the Director.
quote:
The minutes of the meeting of the Executive, convened to con-
sider the budget, were read and the recommendations endorsed
by the meeting. The Secretary/Manager would prepare all the
required detailed documents and forward them to the Director.

summary: The meeting accepted Christie and Sons' $2,838 quotation for re-asphalting the outer courtyard because it was about $500 below A.R.C. Asphalting.
quote:
Of five contractors approached for quotations only two had
responded; one from A.R.C. Asphalting and the other from
Christie and Sons. As the one from Christies' was, at $2838.00,
some $500 below the price quoted by A.R.C. it was decided to
accept the former, especially in view of the fact that
Christies' have a good reputation for the specialised applic-
ation of coloured surfaces.

summary: The proposed charge for parking cars in the grounds was passed to the Grounds Committee for further consideration because of staffing costs and possible effects on the Tea Room trade.
quote:
After some discussion regarding the economics of this pro-
posal which would involve the employment of a collector, and
also the possible adverse effect on the trade at the Tea
Room, it was decided to pass this matter over to the Grounds
Committee for further consideration.

summary: The House Committee was to meet Mr. Lucas to discuss his unresolved kitchen restoration recommendations and matters arising from the architectural survey.
red_flag_reason: The architect's recommendations for the kitchen restoration and development were still unresolved and required further discussion.
quote:
Mr. Herford considered that Mr. Lucas - the architect, was
still "hedging" with his recommendations for the restoration
and development of the kitchen. After some discussion it
was agreed that the House Committee should meet Mr. Lucas
to discuss this matter and also question him regarding
matters arising from the interim report on the architectural
survey. The Secretary/Manager undertook to arrange a mutually
convenient date and time for this meeting.

asset: large dead trees in the park
summary: The Grounds Committee reported that large dead trees too big for staff would be felled by Mr. Lunney and general autumn clearance would continue for three months.
quote:
Mr. Barrett reported that a number of large dead trees,
which were too big to be dealt with by our own staff,
would be felled by Mr. Lunney. General autu mn clearance
had started and would continue during the next three months.
The big clean up of the periphery of the park around the
South Paddock could not be started until we knew the result
of our application for funds for this work under the five
year plan. Likewise re-afforestation could not commence
until the clearing had been completed.

asset: periphery of the park around the South Paddock
summary: The South Paddock clean-up and subsequent re-afforestation were deferred pending the result of the five-year-plan funding application.
red_flag_reason: The South Paddock clean-up and re-afforestation could not start until the result of the five-year-plan funding application was known.
quote:
Mr. Barrett reported that a number of large dead trees,
which were too big to be dealt with by our own staff,
would be felled by Mr. Lunney. General autu mn clearance
had started and would continue during the next three months.
The big clean up of the periphery of the park around the
South Paddock could not be started until we knew the result
of our application for funds for this work under the five
year plan. Likewise re-afforestation could not commence
until the clearing had been completed.

summary: The Legal, Insurance and P.R. Committee advised against hotel and travel-centre micro-film advertising and noted that $2,000 had been applied for in the 1975/76 budget for publicity.
red_flag_reason: Definite allocation of finance was needed to plan a proper publicity campaign, and the Treasurer advised that only $2,000 had been applied for in the 1975/76 budget.
quote:
Furthermore he considered that definite allocation of finance
was necessary to plan a proper publicity campaign. The
Treasurer advised that we had applied for $2,000.00 in the
1975/76 budget and expressed the opinion that our best re-
sults would be obtained by advertising in the appropriate
columns of the Sydney Morning Herald in conjunction with the
President's previous recommendation of taking space in
certain educational magazines.

summary: The Secretary/Manager's circulated report was accepted.
quote: This, having been circulated, was accepted.

summary: Recoup summaries Nos. 61 to 67 were tabled and formally approved by the meeting.
quote:
Recoup summaries Nos. 61 to 67 were tabled and formally
approved by the meeting.

summary: The President was to investigate whether the Trust could qualify for Australian Government restoration grants, while the Secretary/Manager doubted eligibility because the State Government owned Vaucluse House.
red_flag_reason: The Trust's eligibility for Australian Government restoration grants was doubtful because Vaucluse House was owned by the State Government.
quote:
A number of Trustees had recently noticed that quite consider-
able sums of money had been made available by the Australian
Government for restoration of historic buildings and wondered
if the Trust would be eligible for such a grant. The Secretary/
Manager said that as Vaucluse House was owned by the State
Government he was doubtful that we would qualify. However,
the President indicated that he would look into this matter.

summary: Mr. Barrett's request for leave of absence for four months was granted.
quote:
Mr. Barrett advised that he would be absent from the country
during the ensuing four months and requested leave of absence.
This was granted.

summary: Restoration work on the North Wing took longer than anticipated because an interesting West wall feature indicated the verandah roof had once been about two feet lower.
quote:
(i) Restoration work on the North Wing has taken a little longer than
anticipated mainly due to the discovery of an interesting feature in the
West wall, which indicates that the roof over the verandah was at one time
some two feet lower than it is at the present time. We had to keep the area
exposed until Mr. Lucas could arrange for it to be photographed.

asset: stone-work adjacent to the visitors entrance
summary: The Secretary/Manager asked Trustees to view exposed stonework near the visitors' entrance and authorise removal of paint from that wall and under the western verandah to help combat rising damp.
red_flag_reason: Sections of exposed stonework would require restoration, and paint removal was sought to help combat rising damp.
quote:
(ii) An area of stone-work adjacent to the visitors entrance has been
exposed by the removal of numerous layers of paint and I would appreciate it
if you would view this after the meeting with a view to authorising the removal
of all the paint on this wall and right round under the Western side of the
verandah. In the main the stonework exposed is in excellent condition and in
the writers opinion it is aesthetically more pleasing than paint. Undoubtedly
some sections will require restoration, but if done,the walls will once again
be able to breathe and this will materially assist in combating the problem of
rising damp.

summary: New architraves and some frames were fitted in the Reception Room to replace those eaten out by white ants, and the room should reopen within a few days.
quote:
(iii) New architraves and some frames have been fitted in the Reception
Room to replace those eaten out by white ants and the room should be ready
for re-opening to the public within the next few days.

summary: Re-painting of the stables had proceeded well and should be almost completed by the next meeting on 18 May.
quote:
(iv) Re-painting of the stables has proceeded well during the month and
should be almost completed by the time of the next meeting on the 18th. May.

summary: The House Committee met Mr. Lucas on 1 May for almost three hours about the Kitchen area and matters in his interim report.
quote:
(v) The House Committee met Mr. Lucas at the House on the 1st.May and
had almost three hours discussion with him regarding the Kitchen area and
many other matters raised in his interim report. Details will be given to
the Meeting by Messrs. Cook and Herford.

summary: A fresh outbreak of white ant activity in the costume room was treated by Rentokil under contract.
red_flag_reason: A fresh outbreak of white ant activity was discovered in the costume room.
quote:
(vi) A fresh outbreak of white ant activity was discovered in the costume
room and has been treated by Rentokil under our contract.

summary: A Drystat representative was arranged to discuss the rising damp problem with Mr. Lucas, with literature and a company letter to be tabled.
red_flag_reason: A rising damp problem was being discussed with Drystat and Mr. Lucas, indicating a continuing structural/moisture issue.
quote:
(vii) I took advantage of the visit of the House Committee on the 1st. May
by arranging a visit by a representative of Drystat Pty. Limited to discuss our
rising damp problem with them and Mr. Lucas. Literature describing the system
and a letter from the Company will be tabled at the meeting under correspondence.

asset: outer courtyard to the East of the House
summary: Re-asphalting of the outer courtyard east of the House was completed except for final brushing in about four weeks, with other minor asphalting repairs also carried out.
quote:
(i) Re-asphalting of the outer courtyard to the East of the House has
been completed apart from a final brushing over in about four weeks time.
Other minor asphalting repairs have also been carried out whilst Christie's
were on the site.

asset: large dead trees in the Park and tall gums at the gardener's cottage
summary: Eight large dead trees in the Park were felled by Mr. Lunney and three tall gums at the rear of the gardener's cottage were trimmed.
quote:
(ii) Eight large dead trees in the Park have been felled by Mr. Lunney
and three tall gums trimmed at the rear of the gardener's cottage. Mr.
Kearney has spoken very highly of Mr. Lunney's efficiency.

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room
summary: Mr. Clark's $1,500 quotation for trimming the Moreton Bay Fig Tree was received and, with the President's approval, the order for the work was placed.
quote:
(iii) The official quotation from Mr. Clark for the trimming of the
Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room came to hand in the sum of
$1500.00 and with the President's approval the order for the work to be carried
out has been placed. Mr. Clark will proceed as soon as he gets back from a
job he is doing in Darwin.

asset: gates at the North East corner of the Park
summary: Rusted bolts securing the rings in the North East corner gates were replaced where required after the danger of losing them was found.
red_flag_reason: Bolts securing the rings in the North East corner gates had rusted through and there was danger of losing them.
quote:
(iv) On one of my tours of inspection I found that some of the bolts
securing the rings in the gates at the North East corner of the Park had
rusted through and we were in danger of losing them. New bolts have been
fitted where required.

summary: The Secretary/Manager had to warn off youths tearing around the Beach Paddock on trail bikes.
quote:
(v) During the month I have had to "warn off" a number of youths
tearing round the Beach Paddock on trail bikes.

asset: Gas Lamps on the Northern Boundary of the Park
summary: The Australian Gaslight Company was refurbishing the Northern Boundary gas lamps, but might reconsider lighting them if vandalism resumed in winter.
red_flag_reason: The Gaslight Company might reconsider lighting the Northern Boundary gas lamps if vandalism started again in winter.
quote:
(vi) The Australian Gaslight Company have relented regarding their
decision not to light the Gas Lamps on the Northern Boundary of the Park
and they are at the moment re-furbishing them one by one at their workshops
and getting the whole system back into working order again. However, if
vandalism starts again this winter, they may have to re-consider their
decision. I have promised that we will keep our eyes on the lights to the
best of our ability.

summary: Because Mr. Campbell was ill, the Tea Room lease could not be finalised; Mrs. Avenell clarified some points and would discuss the remainder with Mr. Campbell.
red_flag_reason: The Tea Room lease could not be finalised because of Mr. Campbell's prolonged illness, and remaining points still required discussion with him.
quote:
Due to the prolonged illness of Mr. Campbell, it has not been possible
to finalise this matter, although I have had an interview with Mrs. Avenell
and clarified a number of points. The remainder she will discuss with
Mr. Campbell and come back to me as soon as possible. I have kept the
Vice-President and the Service Legal Department advised of these negotiations.

summary: Nielsen Park management and staff were handed over to the District Superintendent on 1 May 1975, former staff were taken over by the Service, and Mrs. Westbrook's long service leave payment remained outstanding with the Public Service Board.
quote:
In accordance with your decision at the last meeting I handed over
the management of Nielsen Park and its staff to the District Superintendent
on the 1st. May 1975. Mr. & Mrs. H. Westbrook departed from Greycliffe
House on the 2nd. <s>April</s> May, so that Mr. Westbrook could take up his appointment
as Senior Ranger-in-Charge, Myall Lakes on the 5th. May. All our former
staff at Nielsen have been taken over by the Service, they have been paid by
us up to the 30th. <s>May</s> May and have been given their tax certificates up to
that date. The only matter outstanding is the long service leave payment
due to Mrs. Westbrook as this is being determined by the Public Service Board.

summary: Nielsen Park Pool admissions before closure on 13 April 1975 produced $339.70 from 1,501 admissions.
Total April revenue was $7,517.86, of which $4,397.56 was due to N.P. & W.S. and $3,120.30 was credited to the Special Purposes Account, more than $1,000 above forecast.
quote:
Total revenue inclusive of admissions,sales, rents etc., was $7517.86
of which, general revenue due to the N.P. & W.S. was $ 4397.56, whilst
$3120.30 was credited to the Special Purposes Account. This latter figure,
due to the high number of admissions for the time of the year coupled with
better than average counter sales, is over $1000.00 more than forecast.
Therefore, the Special Purposes Account is in as healthy a condition as it
was in March despite heavy expenditure during April.

asset: general stores, maintenance of buildings and park facilities
summary: The financial report noted that funds for general stores, building maintenance and park facilities had been exhausted, so those items had to be charged to the Special Purposes Account.
counterparty: Finance Department of the N.P. & W.S.
red_flag_reason: Funds for general stores, building maintenance and park facilities had been exhausted, forcing those items to be charged to the Special Purposes Account.
quote:
Returns from the Finance Department of the N.P. & W.S. show that whilst we
are operating within overall allocations in the General Account for the first
nine months of the current financial year, we have exhausted the funds made available
for general stores, maintenance of buildings and park facilities. Items falling
in these catagories, have therefore, of neccessity had to be charged to the
Special Purposes Account.

summary: The Executive's engagement of Mr. Ralph Clarke to carry out Moreton Bay Fig trimming work was approved.
quote:
<u>(a) Trimming of Moreton Bay Fig</u>
The action of the Executive in engaging Mr. Ralph Clarke to
carry out this work was approved.

summary: The Outer Courtyard re-asphalting was noted as completed, and all members present expressed satisfaction with the work.
quote:
<u>(b) Re-asphalting of Outer Courtyard</u>
It was noted that this had been completed and all members present
expressed satisfaction with the work.

summary: The Alert Alarm Systems quotation for additions to the burglar alarm system was deferred pending reconsideration of Police Department recommendations.
red_flag_reason: A burglar alarm addition quotation was received, but no decision was made until Police Department recommendations were reconsidered.
quote:
(i) A quotation from Alert Alarm Systems for additions to the
burglar alarm system was received, but before making any decis-
ion it was agreed that Mr. Pierce and the Secretary/Manager
should re-consider the recommendations made by the Police
Department at the time the existing system was installed some
four years ago and if considered necessary contact the Police
Department for further recommendations.

summary: The meeting decided to purchase one copy each of Avon Print's 'North View of Sydney, 1824' and 'The Gap, South Head' prints.
quote:
(ii) A circular from Avon Print Pty. Ltd., offering for sale limited
editions of old prints was considered and it was decided to
purchase one copy each of "North View of Sydney, 1824" by J.
Lycett and "The Gap, South Head" by E. Thomas.

summary: Use of the Drawing Room in July for a charitable recital was approved subject to the committee agreeing to security and similar safeguards.
counterparty: Golden Committee of The Royal New South Wales Institute for Deaf and Blind Children
quote:
(iii) A letter from the "Golden Committee" of The Royal New South
Wales Institute for Deaf and Blind Children requesting the use
of the Drawing Room in July for a charitable recital by Geoffrey
Chard, baritone and Geoffrey Parsons, pianist was considered and
subject to this committee agreeing to certain safeguards relating
to security etc., approval was given.

summary: The Director's letter thanking the Trust for cooperation in transferring Nielsen Park administration was noted with satisfaction.
quote:
(iv) A letter from the Director thanking the Trust for its co-operation
in transferring the administration of Nielsen Park into his care
was noted with satisfaction.

summary: In principle, electro-osmosis systems were to be gradually installed in all walls subject to rising damp before re-decoration, following Drystat's discussion.
red_flag_reason: Rising damp in the walls was a continuing problem, and electro-osmosis systems were to be installed in affected walls before re-decoration.
quote:
(v) A letter from Drystat Pty. Ltd., written subsequent to a meeting
of the House Committee with their General Manager, Mr. D.J. van
Dommelen, to discuss the problem of rising damp in the walls was
considered. In view of the fact that a similar system had been
highly successful in controlling rising damp in Gilberthorpe's
Room it was agreed in principle that electro-osmosis systems
should gradually be installed in all walls subject to rising
damp, prior to re-decoration.

summary: The meeting considered the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, noted sections relating to Trustees, and requested six extra copies for Trustees and Counsellors.
quote:
The new Act was considered and special note taken of the
sections relating to Trustees of sites. The Secretary/Manager
was requested to obtain six extra copies so that each Trustee
and Counsellor may have his own copy.

summary: The meeting noted that the new corporate name defined by the Act was 'Trustees of Vaucluse House Historic Site'.
quote:
The meeting noted that the new corporate name as defined by
the Act was "Trustees of Vaucluse House Historic Site".

summary: The Secretary/Manager was authorised to have a new corporate common seal made and to be its custodian.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager was authorised to have a new corporate
common seal made and be custodian thereof.

asset: proof transparencies of the House and ancillary buildings
summary: Members were satisfied with Mr. Thompson's proof transparencies and authorised the Secretary/Manager to phase out the current series and replace it with reproductions from the new proof set.
quote:
The members present expressed satisfaction with the proof
transparencies produced by Mr. Thompson and authorised the
Secretary/Manager to phase out the current series and replace
them with reproductions from the new proof set.

summary: The meeting unanimously approved action on Mr. Lucas' kitchen recommendations, including removing the bricked-up fireplace section, demolishing the draught screening wall, fixing a mantleshelf, restoring the chimney breast, deferring the hood, and acting on the water-storage tank.
quote:
The President tabled a letter which he had received from Mr.
Lucas regarding the kitchen. After the contents of the letter
had been discussed, Mr. Herford moved that action be taken as
follows on Mr. Lucas' recommendations:-

summary: The Grounds Committee reported that dead trees had been felled and autumn clearing and re-planting were proceeding according to schedule.
quote:
Mr. Pierce reported that a number of dead trees had been felled
and that the autumn clearing and re-planting was proceeding
according to schedule.

summary: The tea room lease remained unresolved because Mrs. Avenell could not proceed without Mr. Campbell, and the Vice-President and Legal Department agreed no more could be done at that time.
red_flag_reason: The tea room lease could not be finalised because Mrs. Avenell could not proceed without further consultation with Mr. Campbell, and both the Vice-President and Legal Department agreed no more could be done then.
quote:
The Secretary/Manager reported that in the continuing absence
through illness of Mr. Campbell, Manager of Michael Avenell
Catering Company he had interviewed Mrs. Avenell with a view
to finalising the terms of the lease for the tea room. Some
matters under query had been satisfactorily cleared up, but
with the few remaining, Mrs. Avenell felt that she could not
proceed without further consultation with her partner, Mr.
Campbell. She had promised to clarify the position as soon
as possible.

summary: Trustees considered that a definite policy should be established for commercial filming of the House and Grounds, but deferred detailed discussion until the next meeting when Messrs. Finlay and Doyle were hoped to be present.
quote:
Two subsequent paragraphs dealt with advertising. The first
of these concerned the use of the House and Grounds for filming
by commercial advertisers. Trustees present considered that
with increasing demand a definite policy should be established,
but that detailed discussion should be deferred until the next
meeting when it was hoped that Messrs. Finlay and Doyle would
be present.

summary: The sub-committee was expected shortly to make firm recommendations to the Board regarding an advertising brochure for the site.
quote:
The second indicated that the sub-committee would shortly have
some firm recommendations to make to the Board regarding an
advertising brochure for the site.

summary: Trustees indicated that any application by the Friends to hold a musical soirée in the House would be favourably considered, pending more information.
quote:
The final paragraph of the letter expressed support for the
"Friends" to hold a musical soirée in the House at some future
unspecified time. Trustees present indicated that any application
to hold such a function would be most favourably considered and
looked forward to receiving more information on this proposal.

summary: Members expressed concern about the economic viability of the Tea Room lessees because of Mr. Campbell's illness, and the Secretary/Manager was to ask the bank manager to check M.A.C.C.'s financial soundness.
red_flag_reason: Members were concerned that Mr. Campbell's prolonged illness might affect the economic viability of the Tea Room lessees, and a bank enquiry into M.A.C.C.'s financial soundness was requested.
quote:
Discussion then reverted to the prolonged illness of Mr. Campbell
of M.A.C.C. and some members present expressed concern regarding
the effect of this on the economic viability of the lessees
of the Tea Rooms.

summary: The Secretary/Manager's circulated report was accepted.
quote:
This having been circulated was accepted and in respect of the
rather sudden departure of Mr. Harry Westbrook to take up his

summary: Recoup summaries Nos. 68 to 79 were tabled and formally approved by the meeting.
quote:
Recoup summaries Nos. 68 to 79 were tabled and formally
approved by the meeting.

asset: external wall of the House adjacent to the visitors' entrance
summary: After inspecting experimental paint removal from stonework near the visitors' entrance, the Trustees agreed that, subject to Mr. Lucas's approval, all paint should be removed from that wall and around under the western tower block.
quote:
At the request of the Secretary/Manager the meeting then
adjourned to the House to inspect an experimental removal of
paint from the stonework on the external wall of the House
adjacent to the visitors' entrance. In view of its excellent
state of preservation, it was agreed that subject to the approval
of our architect, Mr. Lucas, all the paint should be removed
from this wall and right around under the western tower block.

summary: The Trustees agreed that no restoration should be carried out in Gilberthorpe's Room until Mr. Lucas had inspected the exposed foundations and taken necessary photographs.
red_flag_reason: Restoration of the exposed foundations in Gilberthorpe's Room was withheld until Mr. Lucas inspected and photographed them.
quote:
The Trustees then examined the interior of the foundations
exposed by the removal of the floor boards and rotten joists
in Gilberthorpe's Room and agreed that no restoration should
be carried out until Mr. Lucas had carried out an inspection
and taken all necessary photographs.

summary: Mrs. P. Hall's ankle took longer to mend than anticipated, and she was not able to resume duties until 26 May.
quote:
Mrs. P. Hall's ankle took a little longer to mend than originally
anticipated and she was not able to resume her duties until the 26th May.

summary: Park worker Mr. T. Whitty resigned at month's end for an appointment with the Indian Government Information Service and was replaced by Mr. Thomas Hughes.
counterparty: Mr. T. Whitty and Mr. Thomas Hughes
quote:
Park worker, Mr. T. Whitty resigned his position at the end of the
month to take up an appointment in Sydney with the Indian Government
Information Service. He has been replaced by Mr. Thomas Hughes, an ex-
perienced gardener formerly with St. Catherine's School as gardener/
handyman for 8½ years. It is hoped that he will prove to be a valuable
assistant to the Head Gardener.

summary: Restoration work on the North Wing was completed, and repainting of the walls in stone-coloured matt acrylic paint was being carried out.
quote:
(1) Restoration work on the North Wing has been completed and re-paint-
ing of the walls in a stone coloured matt acrylic paint as recommended by
Mr. Lucas is being carried out.

summary: The costume case from the China Room and display case from the second-floor landing were transferred to the new museum area in the Stables.
quote:
(2) The costume case from the China Room and the display case from the
end of the second floor landing in the west wing have been transferred
to the new museum area in the Stables.

summary: Mr. Lucas requested that new joists and re-flooring in Gilberthorpe's Room not be installed until he had researched his findings and resolved his doubts about the room's original use.
red_flag_reason: Mr. Lucas had grave doubts about the room's original use and requested that new joists and re-flooring not be installed until he had thought and researched his findings.
quote:
(3) Mr. Lucas, after examining the foundations in "Gilberthorpe's Room"
has requested that we do not instal the new joists and re-floor until
he has had time to think about his findings and done some research work.
He has very grave doubts if this room was a bed-sitting room at all
originally.

summary: The external woodwork of the Boardroom was repaired and repainted to match that on the stables.
quote:
(4) The external woodwork of the Boardroom has been repaired and repainted
to match that on the stables.

summary: The Costume Room case damaged by white ants had been repaired.
quote:
(5) The case in the Costume Room which was damaged by white ants has been
repaired.

asset: patchwork quilt in Miss Wentworth's room
summary: Experts pronounced the patchwork quilt irrepairable, and Mrs. Kiernan proposed covering it with fine transparent net if the Trust approved.
red_flag_reason: Experts pronounced the patchwork quilt irrepairable because the original material could not be matched and existing fabrics were too delicate to stitch.
quote:
(6) The patchwork quilt on the bed in Miss Wentworth's room has, through
the good offices of Mrs. G. Kiernan been examined by experts at the School
of Needlework who have pronounced it irrepairable as the type of material,
used originally, cannot be matched to-day and the existing fabrics are
so delicate that they would "tear away" as soon as a thread was put into
them. In an attempt to preserve the quilt and hold it together Mrs. Kiernan
will, if the Trust approves, cover it with a fine transparent net which will
permit the colours of the fabrics to "show through".

asset: Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room
summary: Mr. Ralph Clarke had commenced surgery on the Moreton Bay Fig Tree, with about twenty-five tonnes of timber expected to be removed and small branches chipped for weed control.
quote:
(i) Mr. Ralph Clarke has commenced surgery on the Moreton Bay Fig Tree
adjacent to the Tea Room; it is anticipated that eventually the weight
of timber removed will be in the region of twenty-five tonnes. All small
branches are being put through the "chipper" thus providing a useful
stock-pile of chips for weed control around bushes in the formal gardens.

(ii) The trunks of trees felled by Mr. Lunney have been trimmed and cut
into suitable lengths for use as natural-looking barriers surrounding the
public car park and to prevent cars being driven into other areas where

red_flag_reason: Soil compaction is damaging tree roots and shortening tree life.

summary: The Secretary/Manager examined convict-cut dressed stone from cottages being demolished in Pitt Street, Redfern, estimated that about 15 tons could be made available, and noted that it would be valuable for future restorations except for transport costs.
quote:
At the request of the President I examined the stone foundations of a row
of cottages in Pitt Street, Redfern which are being demolished by Mr.
Blackman and have "ear-marked " it for the Trust. Mr. Blackman showed
me markings on the stone which almost certainly prove that the stone was
cut and dressed by convicts in the early part of the 19th century. In
the writer's opinion it will be most valuable in carrying out future
restorations to the fabric of the House. It is estimated that about
15 tons of the stone will be made available to us. There will be no
charge for it apart from the cost of transport.

summary: Brian D. Thornton offered an 1868 open carriage originally owned by the MacArthur Family on permanent loan, and the offer was accepted subject to Trust approval.
quote:
"Out of the blue" a Mr. Brian D. Thornton of Mosman telephoned the writer
and asked if the Trust would like to have this carriage on permanent loan.
At the instigation of the President, Mr. Herford and the writer arranged
to view the carriage which is in very fair condition and subject to Trust
approval the offer has been accepted. It is considered that this carriage
will constitute a much more appropriate exhibit in the Coachhouse than
the Cobb & Co. Coach.

summary: Two mid-19th century hanging lamps were purchased through Mr. P. Cook with the President's approval to replace globes in the china and period costume rooms.
quote:
Through the good offices of Mr. P. Cook and with the approval of the
President, two very fine mid-19th century hanging lamps have been purchased
to replace the two nondescript globes in the china and period costume rooms.
Whilst "rummaging" in the loft over the Boardroom the writer found a very
ornate, but dirty and damaged hall lamp of mid-19th century design. I
think it can be restored and used to replace the 20th centry globe in the
hall between the courtyard and the kitchen.

summary: A small polished 19th century Australian cedar hall table was acquired to fill the space in the west wing first-floor corridor after the information case was removed to the museum.
quote:
A small polished 19th century Australian cedar hall table has also been
acquired to fill the space left at the end of the first floor corridor
in the west wing when the information case was removed to the museum.

Sydney" by Joseph Lycett have been purchased from Avon Fine Prints and
are being suitably framed.

quote:
(a) Arising from the quotation for a supplementary burglar alarm system,
it was agreed that the somewhat obtrusive red fire alarm bell should
be overpainted in a stone colour.

summary: Trustees requested copies of new colour 35 mm transparencies for an advertising brochure, and the Secretary/Manager agreed to approach the Interpretations Division of N.P. & W.S. to make suitable transparencies available after printers finished with them.
quote:
(b) Messrs. Finlay and Doyle requested that when available, copies of the
new colour 35 mm transparencies be obtained for use in the advertising
brochure they are preparing. The Secretary/Manager suggested that the
5" x 3" transparencies used in the preparation of the new series of
post cards and coloured letter-card folder would reproduce better in
a brochure and undertook to approach the Interpretations Division
of N.P. & W.S. with a view to these being made available when the
