summary: The President read a thank-you letter to Harry Westbrook for services to the Trust since 1955, and the meeting heartily approved its contents.
quote:
(c) The President read a copy of the letter which he had sent to Mr. Harry
Westbrook thanking them for their services to the Trust since 1955.
The meeting heartily approved of the contents of this letter.

asset: stone walls adjacent to the visitors' entrance
summary: The Secretary/Manager reported that architect Mr. Clive Lucas had examined the stone walls adjacent to the visitors' entrance, approved removal of existing paint, and work was proceeding.
quote:
(d) The Secretary/Manager reported that, in accordance with instructions
received, the stone walls adjacent to the visitors' entrance had been
examined by the architect Mr. Clive Lucas, who had approved of the
complete removal of existing paint. Work was therefore proceeding.

summary: The Trustees reviewed correspondence with the Friends of Vaucluse House, concurred with the President's reply, and resolved on information-sharing, formal communication, personal contact, formal Friends meetings, member involvement, project comments, confidentiality of minutes, and written conveyance of the resolutions.
quote:
(i) The President read to the meeting a long letter he had received from
the Secretary of the "Friends of Vaucluse House", and followed this up
by reading the reply he had felt it necessary to write. The Trustees
present fully concurred with the contents of the President's letter
which had resulted in a meeting between representatives of the Trust
and committee members of the "Friends" which had clarified the basic
relationship between the two bodies and, it was hoped, laid the found-
ation for a better understanding between them.

summary: The meeting found that Mr. Lucas had misunderstood the architectural survey cost ceiling of $3,000.00, that invoices exceeded that figure by about $1,900.00, and resolved that the President and Secretary/Manager interview Mr. Lucas and seek agreement.
red_flag_reason: Architectural survey invoices exceeded the agreed $3,000 ceiling by about $1,900.
quote:
(ii) The President tabled a letter he had received from Mr. Lucas the
architect, together with invoices received by the Secretary/Manager
indicating that he had misunderstood instructions received regarding
the "ceiling" cost of the architectural survey.
The meeting reviewed the relevant correspondence and unanimously
agreed that the Secretary/Manager's letter of the 11th April, 1975
was quite clear and unequivocal in stating that the cost of the
survey was not to exceed $3,000.00.
In view of the fact that the invoices submitted exceeded this figure by
some $1900.00 three Trustees initially expressed the view that the
Trust should sever its connection with the firm of Fisher, Lucas
forthwith. However, after further discussion it was resolved that
the President and the Secretary/Manager should interview Mr. Lucas
and be empowered to reach an agreement with him.

summary: Permission was granted for Miss Diane Armstrong's forthcoming marriage to take place in the grounds on Saturday, 19th July at noon.
quote:
(iii) A letter was received from a Miss Diane Armstrong requesting per-
mission for her forthcoming marriage to take place in the grounds on
Saturday, 19th July at noon. Permission was granted.

summary: The President read a personal letter from Captain Lusher, and all members present asked him to send their kindest regards to Captain Lusher and his wife when replying.
quote:
(iv) The President read a personal letter which he had received from
Captain Lusher (RAN Ret'd) - a former Trustee. All members present
asked the President to send their kindest regards to Captain Lusher
and his wife when replying.

summary: Despite an objection from the Friends committee, the meeting unanimously agreed not to rescind the decision to permit the concert in the Drawing Room organised by the Golden Committee of the Royal N.S.W. Institute for Blind and Deaf Children.
counterparty: Golden Committee of the Royal N.S.W. Institute for Blind and Deaf Children
quote:
<u>(a) Concert in Drawing Room.</u>
Despite an objection raised by the Committee of the "Friends", it was
unanimously agreed that the decision to permit this concert, which
was being organised by the "Golden Committee" of the Royal N.S.W.
Institute for Blind and Deaf Children, should not be rescinded.

summary: The Trustees unanimously accepted the loan of the 1868 open carriage from Brian D. Thornton and instructed the Secretary/Manager to arrange its value for insurance and the proposed minimum loan period.
quote:
<u>(b) Offer of 1868 Open Carriage</u>
It was unanimously agreed to accept the generous offer of the loan
of this coach, formerly owned by the Macarthur Family, from Mr.
Brien D. Thornton of Mosman. The Secretary/Manager was instructed
to make all necessary arrangements with Mr. Thornton and in particular
ascertain its value for insurance purposes and the proposed minimum
period of the loan.

summary: The Trustees accepted the offer of old dressed stone from demolition contractor Mr. Blackmore and agreed to thank Mr. K.W. Hodgetts for advising them of the restoration material.
quote:
The Trustees accepted with great pleasure this offer from the demol-
ition contractor, Mr. Blackmore and also agreed that a letter of
thanks be sent to Mr. K.W. Hodgetts of Woollahra for his public
spirited action in advising us of the availability of this excellent
restoration material.

summary: The House Committee requested Trust approval to purchase a simple pine bench, circa 1865, for $85.00 for the kitchen, and approval was given.
quote:
Mr. Herford reported on progress made in the kitchen area and requested
Trust approval to purchase for $85.00 a simple pine bench, circa 1865,
which he felt would be eminently suitable for the kitchen. Approval
was given.

summary: The Secretary/Manager reported progress with trimming the large Moreton Bay Fig Tree and other general winter clearing in the grounds.
quote:
As Mr. Barrett and Mr. Pierce were unavoidably absent from the meeting,
the Secretary/Manager briefly reported progress being made in connection
with the trimming of the big Moreton Bay Fig Tree and other general
winter clearing in the grounds.

summary: The President suggested that the Trust purchase a copy of 'The English Garden' to study gardens possibly existing in Wentworth's day, and purchase was approved.
quote:
In order to study more closely the type of garden possibly existing
in Wentworth's day, the President suggested that the Trust should
purchase a book entitled "The English Garden" a copy of which had
recently been lent to him by Mr. Snelling. Purchase was approved.

summary: The Vice-President reported that he had interviewed Mrs. Avenell again about the tea room lease and that all parties were now in agreement regarding its format.
quote:
The Vice-President reported that he had interviewed Mrs. Avenell
again regarding the lease of the tea room and all parties were now in
agreement regarding its format.

summary: The Museum Committee reported progress preparing exhibits and noted that Miss Yvonne Brown had been asked to investigate matters and was expected to supply requested information soon.
quote:
Mr. Snelling reported on the progress made in the preparation of
exhibits.

summary: Because the School of Needlework said the patchwork quilt from Miss Wentworth's Bedroom was too delicate to repair, the meeting accepted Mrs. Kiernan's offer to attempt to preserve it with a covering of fine net.
red_flag_reason: The patchwork quilt was too delicate to repair, requiring preservation instead.
quote:
It was agreed, that in view of the information received from the
School of Needlework that the patchwork quilt from "Miss Wentworth's
Bedroom" was too delicate to repair, that Mrs. Kiernan's offer to
attempt to preserve it with a covering of fine net be gratefully
accepted.

summary: The remainder of the Secretary/Manager's report was approved and accepted.
quote: The remainder of the report was approved and accepted.

summary: Recoup summaries Nos. 80 to 89 were tabled and formally accepted by the meeting.
quote:
Recoup summaries Nos. 80 to 89 were tabled and formally accepted
by the meeting.

summary: The President reported that the Director thought a substantial Commonwealth Government grant for restoration work would probably be favourably considered, and the matter was deferred for fuller discussion at the July meeting.
quote:
The President advised that he had approached the Director regarding
the feasibility of obtaining a substantial grant from the Commonwealth
Government for restoration work. The Director was of the opinion
that an application for such a grant would probably be favourably
considered. It was agreed that this matter should be discussed
more fully at the July meeting.

summary: After viewing the partly opened-up fireplace and area where the wind-break had been removed, Trustees agreed that further opening of the fireplace should be carried out as approved by the architect.
quote: The Trustees then adjourned to the kitchen to view the partly

asset: plaster and render around the stove in the scullery
summary: The meeting agreed that an investigatory removal of plaster and render around the stove in the scullery should be undertaken.
quote:
"opened up" fireplace and the area from which the wind-break
had been removed. All present expressed great satisfaction with the
improved appearance of the kitchen resulting from the work. It was
agreed that some further opening up of the fireplace as approved
by the architect should be carried out and that an investigatory
removal of some plaster and render around the stove in the scullery
should be undertaken.

summary: The June 1975 report noted that Government auditors were present from 24 June to 8 July and, apart from a few suggestions, appeared satisfied with the way the books were being kept.
quote:
The presence of the Government auditors from the 24th June to the 8th
July, coupled with squaring off the General Account at the end of the
financial year has, of necessity, involved the Secretariat in a fair
amount of extra work during that period. Apart from a few suggestions
aimed at making their work easier next time the auditors appeared to be
satisfied with the way the books are being kept. The fact that they com-
pleted their work in a fortnight as opposed to the three months it took
them to sort things out at the last audit shortly after my appointment in
1973, indicates that we are now running on the right lines. The implement-
ation of their suggestions will I hope enable them to complete future
audits inside a week.

summary: There were no staff changes during June, although some grounds staff were absent sick for short periods.
quote:
There have been no staff changes during the month. Some members of the
grounds staff have been absent sick for short periods during the month.

summary: Mr. and Mrs. John Kearney were scheduled to proceed on leave for three weeks commencing Friday, 18 July 1975.
quote:
Mr. and Mrs. John Kearney will proceed on leave for three weeks commencing
on Friday, 18th July, 1975

summary: Repainting of the walls under the north wing verandah had been completed.
quote: (1) Repainting of the walls under the north wing verandah has been completed.

summary: Paint removable by blow-lamp had been stripped from the west tower block stonework, with the remainder being removed by other methods, and Mr. Lucas was pleased with the results so far.
quote:
(2) All paint that could be removed with a blow-lamp has been stripped from
the stonework of the west tower block. The remainder is being removed by
various other methods. Mr. Lucas has expressed himself as being very pleased
with the results so far.

summary: The draught-screen or wind-break adjacent to the kitchen chimney breast and much infilling brickwork in the original fireplace had been demolished in stages so Mr. Lucas could examine the material removed.
quote:
(3) The draught-screen or wind-break adjacent to the kitchen chimney breast
has been demolished together with much of the infilling brickwork in the ori-
ginal fireplace. This work is being carried out in stages so that Mr. Lucas -
the architect can make a detailed examination of the material removed.

summary: Paint and plaster had been removed around the fuel stove in the scullery, revealing a large infilling of brick that suggested an open fireplace, and Mr. Lucas was to examine the work and kitchen fireplace on 18 July 1975.
quote:
(4) An area of paint and plaster has been removed from around the fuel stove
in the scullery. As in the kitchen a large infilling of brick has been re-
vealed and everything points to this having also been an open fireplace when
Wentworth built the kitchens. Mr. Lucas is to examine this work and the
kitchen fireplace on Friday, 18th July, 1975.

summary: Mr. Davis from the Technological Museum examined the hot water storage tank in the kitchen and would submit a report and attempt to ascertain the age of the ranges in the kitchen and scullery.
quote:
(5) The hot water storage tank in the kitchen has been examined by a Mr.
Davis from the staff of the Technological Museum and he will be submitting
his report in due course. He will also attempt to ascertain the age of the
ranges in the kitchen and scullery.

summary: The President and Secretary of the Australian Antique Arms Society examined the collection of swords and firearms and offered to repair and refurbish them free of charge with technical reports on each weapon.
quote:
(6) Our collection of swords and firearms have been examined by the President
and Secretary of the Australian Antique Arms Society. They have offered
to personally repair and re-furbish them free of charge and to give a technical
report on each weapon.

summary: Mr. and Mrs. Weekes collected the two dining chairs with blue seat covers from the Guests' Dining Room that they had loaned to the Trust.
quote:
(7) Mr. and Mrs. Weekes who are back in Sydney for three months have collected
the two dining chairs with blue seat covers from the Guests' Dining Room
which they had loaned to the Trust. They did not match the Dining Room suite
and I personally think the room looks better without them.

summary: Stocks of the new coloured folder with eleven views of the House and grounds had been received from Roden Print and were on sale.
quote:
(8) Stocks of the new coloured folder with eleven views of the House and
grounds have been received from Roden Print and are now on sale. A sample
will be provided at the next meeting for examination.

summary: Detective Sergeant Filewood of the N.S.W. police had examined the present security system in the House and would submit his report and recommendations soon.
quote:
(9) Detective Sergeant Filewood of the N.S.W. police has examined the present
security system in the House and will be submitting his report and recommend-
ations in the near future.

summary: Because of inclement weather and soft ground, Mr. Ralph Clarke had not been able to complete trimming the Moreton Bay Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room until the ground could support the 20-tonne crane.
red_flag_reason: Tree trimming was delayed because soft ground could not support the 20-tonne crane.
quote:
(i) Due to inclement weather and the resulting softness of the ground Mr.
Ralph Clarke has not been able to complete the trimming of the Moreton Bay
Fig Tree adjacent to the Tea Room. As soon as the ground is hard enough to
take the 20 tonne weight of the crane, he will finish the job.

summary: Storms during June resulted in the loss of five more trees and many broken branches, and grounds staff took almost a fortnight to complete clean-up.
red_flag_reason: Storms caused loss of five trees and broken branches, requiring almost a fortnight of clean-up.
quote:
(ii) Storms during the month resulted in the loss of five more trees and the
breaking of many branches. It took the grounds staff almost a fortnight
to effect a complete "clean-up".

summary: New planting and much pruning had been carried out, and despite bad weather and extra work the gardens were expected to look quite good for the time of year.
quote:
(iii) New planting and much pruning has been carried out. Despite a long
spell of bad weather and the resultant extra work this has involved, I think
Trustees will find the gardens looking quite good for the time of the year.

summary: The Secretary/Manager advised Mr. Lucas not to proceed further with the architectural survey, and after the 2 June interview about his excessive account, the President was to report to the Board on 20 July 1975.
red_flag_reason: The survey was stopped because of an excessive account rendered for architectural services.
quote:
In accordance with your instructions at the last meeting I advised Mr. Lucas,
in writing, not to proceed any further with the survey. On the 2nd June
Mr. Lucas was interviewed by the President and the writer regarding the ex-
cessive account he had rendered for his services. The President will report
on this meeting to the Board on the 20th July, 1975.

summary: The June 1975 financial report stated that known committed expenditure required $1,418.66 more than was available in the Special Purposes Account because the Consultant Architect exceeded the architectural survey allocation, with July revenue expected to make up the projected deficit if no further commitments were made for one month.
red_flag_reason: Known committed expenditure exceeded the Special Purposes Account by $1,418.66 because the Consultant Architect exceeded the architectural survey allocation.
quote:
Therefore, the approximate amount required to enable the Trust to meet known
committed expenditure is $1418.66 in excess of what is currently available in
the Special Purposes Account. This situation is entirely due to the Consultant
Architect exceeding the amount allocated for the architectural survey. July
revenue should make up this projected deficit providing no further commitments
are entered into for a period of one month.
